issues.title: SpriteEffect caches a MatrixTransform parameter that never exists, so OnApply() never sets the sprite projection
issues.summary: SpriteEffect looks up a MatrixTransform parameter its base Effect never creates, so Parameters["MatrixTransform"] is null and OnApply() returns before computing the orthographic projection and half-pixel offset.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Graphics::SpriteEffect: its MatrixTransform parameter and OnApply()
issues.expected: CNA's own SpriteEffect header documents the class as applying "a single world-view-projection matrix transform to a textured quad" and its OnApply() as applying "the sprite transform matrix parameter to the graphics device". OnApply() in SpriteEffect.cpp computes exactly that (Matrix::CreateOrthographicOffCenter over the viewport, multiplied after Matrix::CreateTranslation(-0.5f, -0.5f, 0.0f)). Note on XNA: XNA 4.0 has no public SpriteEffect type; its SpriteBatch owns a private Effect built from an embedded SpriteEffectCode blob and sets that effect's MatrixTransform parameter itself in PrepRenderState. A public SpriteEffect with a MatrixTransform parameter that Apply() fills is therefore a CNA class, not an XNA 4.0 contract.
issues.actual: Both constructors call SpriteEffect::CacheEffectParameters(), which stores getParametersProperty()["MatrixTransform"]. Nothing ever adds a parameter of that name: Effect::Effect(GraphicsDevice&) adds only a technique named Default, and SpriteEffect adds no parameter. EffectParameterCollection::operator[](const std::string&) returns nullptr for an absent name, so matrixParam_ is always null and OnApply() returns at its first statement. Code that reads effect.getParametersProperty()["MatrixTransform"] on a SpriteEffect receives a null pointer, and Apply() never computes the projection its own documentation describes.

sources.note: SpriteEffect::CacheEffectParameters (lookup of MatrixTransform) and SpriteEffect::OnApply (early return on a null parameter)
class SpriteEffect: matrixParam_ and the class comment
Effect::Effect(GraphicsDevice&) adds only the Default technique
EffectParameterCollection::operator[](const std::string&) returns nullptr for an unknown name
only Clone() and Apply()-does-not-throw are tested
cna_sprite_effect_create: the generated route, the only in-tree creator outside tests

issues.evidence:
Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; not executed. No renderer consumes the SpriteEffect class: the renderers that run XNA's sprite shader (for example D3D9SpriteBatch.cpp and SoftwareSpriteBatch.cpp) load their own embedded compiled SpriteEffect.fxb and look up MatrixTransform in that blob, and SpriteBatch.cpp never instantiates the class. Its only in-tree creator outside tests is the C API's cna_sprite_effect_create. The defect is therefore latent for ordinary SpriteBatch drawing and visible to code that instantiates SpriteEffect directly.

Independently observed as a separate finding (merged): CacheEffectParameters looks the name up on an effect that has no parameters, matrixParam_ stays null and OnApply returns before building XNA's half-pixel orthographic projection; renderers supply sprite projection themselves, so ordinary drawing is unaffected.

Independent re-verification: Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; not executed. No renderer consumes the SpriteEffect class: the renderers that run XNA's sprite shader (for example D3D9SpriteBatch.cpp and SoftwareSpriteBatch.cpp) load their own embedded compiled SpriteEffect.fxb and look up MatrixTransform in that blob, and SpriteBatch.cpp never instantiates the class. Its only in-tree creator outside tests is the C API's cna_sprite_effect_create. The defect is therefore latent for ordinary SpriteBatch drawing and visible only to code that instantiates SpriteEffect directly; because XNA 4.0 has no public SpriteEffect, that code is CNA-specific (C++ or the C API), not ported XNA code. XNA's own SpriteBatch keeps the MatrixTransform parameter on a private Effect and sets it itself.
issues.reproduction:
// Illustrative; not compiled or run for this entry.
using namespace Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Graphics;
GraphicsDevice device;
SpriteEffect effect(device);
EffectParameter* transform = effect.getParametersProperty()["MatrixTransform"];
// XNA 4.0: a Matrix parameter that Apply() fills with halfPixelOffset * projection.
// CNA at 3b43bd86: transform == nullptr, and effect.Apply() computes nothing.
effect.Apply();
issues.tests_current: SpriteEffectTests.cpp has CloneReturnsIndependentSpriteEffect and CloneAndOriginalApplyIndependently (Apply() does not throw). Neither asserts that the parameter exists or that Apply() writes a value.
issues.regression_test: A SpriteEffectTests.cpp case asserting that getParametersProperty()["MatrixTransform"] is non-null and, after Apply() on a device with a known viewport, holds CreateTranslation(-0.5, -0.5, 0) * CreateOrthographicOffCenter(0, width, height, 0, 0, 1).
issues.blast_radius: Code that constructs SpriteEffect directly (C++ or cna_sprite_effect_create) and reads, sets or relies on MatrixTransform, for example XNA code ported unchanged. Ordinary SpriteBatch drawing is unaffected because each renderer supplies the sprite transform itself; the C API's cna_effect_is_exact_stock_sprite_effect identity query is unaffected.
issues.workaround: Do not rely on SpriteEffect's MatrixTransform; ordinary SpriteBatch drawing needs no explicit SpriteEffect.

issues.title: Load<Song> and Load<Video> resolve a same-named .cnj file and return a media object that points at JSON
issues.summary: ResolveAssetPath tries name.cnj before the Song and Video readers' media extensions, and neither reader handles .cnj, so a same-named .cnj silently becomes the Song or Video file.
issues.public_contract: ContentManager::Load for Media::Song and Media::Video (the loose-file tier)
issues.expected: The .cnj-first rule (a sidecar has the final say over a native file of the same name) is meant for readers that understand a .cnj envelope. Load<Song> and Load<Video> should either skip a .cnj candidate and reach the media file, or refuse it with a ContentLoadException naming the .cnj. They must never hand back a Song or Video whose file is a JSON document: XNA's contract for Load<T> is a usable asset or a ContentLoadException.
issues.actual:
After the compiled tiers miss, ResolveAssetPath ({{src:modules/content/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ContentManager.hpp|ContentManager.hpp}}) returns the literal path if it exists, then name.cnj if it exists, and only then tries the reader's GetExtensions(). SongTypeReader::Read and VideoTypeReader::Read ({{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentMediaLoaders.cpp|ContentMediaLoaders.cpp}}) have no .cnj branch: they construct Media::Song(path, stem) and Media::Video(path, device) from whatever path they are given. Song::Song ({{src:modules/media/src/Xna/Song.cpp|Song.cpp}}) only checks that the file exists. Video::Video ({{src:modules/media/src/Xna/Video/Video.cpp|Video.cpp}}) checks existence, requires a video decoder, and when VideoDecoder::Open fails on the JSON it silently leaves width, height and duration at zero.

So with Content/theme.cnj and Content/theme.ogg side by side, Load<Song>("theme") succeeds and returns a Song whose handle is theme.cnj; the failure appears only at MediaPlayer::Play, far from its cause. Load<Video> returns a 0×0, zero-length Video in a build with FFmpeg (in a decoder-free build it fails anyway, with a wrapped NotSupportedException). Texture2D, TextureCube and SoundEffect are not affected: their readers branch on a .cnj path.

sources.note: ContentManager::ResolveAssetPath - literal, then .cnj, then reader extensions
SongTypeReader::Read and VideoTypeReader::Read - no .cnj branch
Song::Song(std::string, std::string) - existence check only
Video::Video(std::string, GraphicsDevice*) - probe failure leaves zero metadata

issues.evidence:
Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; the Song half was also executed (see below), the Video half was not. No Song or Video .cnj envelope type exists in {{tree:modules/content/src|the content module}} (the only Song and Video formats are the .xnb readers and the .cnb media codec), so no valid .cnj can be meant for these two readers. An earlier review described this defect as narrowed because the .xnb and .cnb tiers take precedence; they do, but they were never part of it: the compiled tiers run first, so the misresolution is confined to the loose tier. What MediaPlayer::Play reports for a JSON file depends on the audio backend's decoder and was not checked.

Independent re-verification: Reproduced for Song by the audit at 009d40f5; the Video half was checked by reading only. That commit's ContentManager and Song sources were compiled with g++ -O0 (headless renderer macro, headless platform installed) into a probe with Content/theme.ogg (empty) and Content/theme.cnj (a small JSON envelope) side by side: Load<Song>("theme") returned a Song whose handle ended in theme.cnj without throwing, while Load<Song>("theme.ogg") returned the .ogg. The sharp-runtime types came from a sibling checkout that TARGET does not pin. No Song or Video .cnj envelope type exists in the content module, and {{src:docs/cnj-format.md|docs/cnj-format.md}}, the .cnj specification that replaced misc/cnj.md, tries .cnj before every type's native extensions and defines no Song or Video document (its sourceFile table refuses the member for every built-in type but Texture2D, SoundEffect and TextureCube). What MediaPlayer::Play reports for a JSON file depends on the audio backend's decoder and was not checked.
issues.reproduction:
Illustrative; the Song half was executed by the audit (see Evidence).

// Content/theme.ogg is a real song; Content/theme.cnj is any .cnj document,
// for example a game-defined data record loaded elsewhere with RegisterCnjLoader.
ContentManager content(&services, "Content");
Media::Song song = content.Load<Media::Song>("theme");  // succeeds
// song.getHandle() ends in "theme.cnj", not "theme.ogg"
Media::MediaPlayer::Play(&song);                         // fails here instead
issues.tests_current: {{src:modules/content/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/CnjResolverOrderTests.cpp|CnjResolverOrderTests.cpp}} pins the .cnj-first rule, but only for Texture2D, whose reader understands .cnj. {{src:modules/content/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ContentManagerSongXnbTests.cpp|ContentManagerSongXnbTests.cpp}} and {{src:modules/content/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ContentManagerVideoXnbTests.cpp|ContentManagerVideoXnbTests.cpp}} cover the .xnb tier. No test puts a .cnj beside a media file.
issues.regression_test: A CnjResolverOrderTests case that writes theme.cnj (any valid envelope) and a short theme.wav, then requires Load<Song>("theme").getHandle() to end in .wav, or the load to throw ContentLoadException, whichever the fix chooses. Song construction needs no audio device, so the test runs headless. The Video twin needs an FFmpeg build and would check getFileNameProperty().
issues.blast_radius: Only Load<Song> and Load<Video> on the loose tier, and only when a same-named .cnj exists in the same directory. Compiled .xnb/.cnb songs and videos, and every other built-in type, are unaffected.
issues.workaround: Give .cnj files names that no song or video shares, or load media with an explicit extension (Load<Song>("theme.ogg")), which the literal-path step resolves first.

issues.title: GraphicsDeviceCapabilityTest's catch-all expectations are still wrong for STUB and for Linux SDL_GPU builds without libshaderc
issues.summary: ExpectedCapabilities() now has an SDL_GPU arm, but on Linux it keeps the catch-all custom-effects expectation true although an SDL_GPU build without libshaderc answers false, and STUB, which answers false to every capability, still takes the all-true default.
issues.public_contract: GraphicsDeviceCapabilityTest.SupportsOcclusionQuery, SupportsCustomEffects and SupportsMultipleRenderTargets (ExpectedCapabilities())
issues.expected: A renderer that truthfully reports a capability as false should pass the shared capability suite. ExpectedCapabilities() in GraphicsDeviceCapabilityTests.cpp exists to state each renderer's accepted boundary, so every renderer whose answers differ from the all-true catch-all needs an arm that says so.
issues.actual: ExpectedCapabilities() has explicit arms for FNA3D, SOFTWARE and SDL_GPU; every other renderer takes default: return {true, true, true}. The SDL_GPU arm expects occlusion queries false everywhere and custom effects false on Apple, Windows and Emscripten, but on other hosts it keeps the default true, because whether the build found libshaderc is visible only to the renderer target (CNA_SDL_GPU_SHADER_EFFECTS is a private definition) and SdlGpuRenderer::SupportsCapability(CustomEffects) answers false without it; SupportsCustomEffects therefore fails in a Linux SDL_GPU build without libshaderc. STUB answers false to every capability (StubRenderer::SupportsCapability) and still takes the catch-all, so SupportsOcclusionQuery, SupportsCustomEffects and the HiDef half of SupportsMultipleRenderTargets expect true on STUB.

sources.note: ExpectedCapabilities(): the SDL_GPU arm and the default arm; SupportsOcclusionQuery, SupportsCustomEffects, SupportsMultipleRenderTargets
CNA_SDL_GPU_SHADER_EFFECTS: a private definition, only with a target-native libshaderc
SdlGpuRenderer::SupportsCapability: CustomEffects follows CNA_SDL_GPU_SHADER_EFFECTS
StubRenderer::SupportsCapability returns false for every capability

issues.evidence:
Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; not executed. CNA's records at c1c316b9 showed the catch-all failing five cases under STUB (integration/BATCH_1_STABILIZATION.md, no longer in the tree at 3b43bd86); no CNA record of GraphicsDeviceCapabilityTest.* in a Linux SDL_GPU build without libshaderc was found.

Narrowed at c1c316b9: bb9250261 (AM4-070) rewrote sdlgpu_occlusionquery_limitation_test.cpp to assert the public constructor's NotSupportedException and the renderer's exact message at its own query factory, so that test no longer contradicts the renderer; e5a943e0d (AM4-175) gave ExpectedCapabilities() its SDL_GPU arm (occlusion queries false everywhere, custom effects false on Apple, Windows and Emscripten). Read at 3b43bd86; not executed.

Re-verified at c6dec91f: ExpectedCapabilities() keeps the FNA3D, SOFTWARE and SDL_GPU arms and the all-true default, and StubRenderer::SupportsCapability still returns false for every capability. Not executed.
issues.reproduction:
# Not executed for this entry. A Linux SDL_GPU build with tests and without libshaderc, or a STUB build with tests:
ctest --test-dir <build> -R 'GraphicsDeviceCapabilityTest\.Supports(CustomEffects|OcclusionQuery|MultipleRenderTargets)$' --output-on-failure
issues.tests_current: GraphicsDeviceCapabilityTests.cpp (per-renderer expectations; its MRT case also compares the capability with a real two-target bind) and sdlgpu_occlusionquery_limitation_test.cpp (now consistent with the renderer). Nothing checks that ExpectedCapabilities() has an arm for every renderer whose answers differ from the catch-all.
issues.regression_test: Give ExpectedCapabilities() an explicit STUB arm (all false), and let the SDL_GPU arm see whether the shader-effect route was built (a public compile definition, or ask the renderer's custom-effect intake directly). A structural guard in the style of TheMultipleRenderTargetCapabilityMatchesWhatBindingActuallyDoes for CustomEffects would catch the next mismatch.
issues.blast_radius: Test evidence only; renderer behaviour is correct. STUB runs of the shared capability suite and Linux SDL_GPU runs without libshaderc report failures that are not renderer defects, which inflates their failure counts and can hide real regressions among them.
issues.workaround: When triaging such a run, treat these failures as test defects.

issues.title: The .cnj JSON parser (CNA::Internal::ParseJson) recurses without a nesting limit, so a small crafted document overflows the stack
issues.summary: JsonParser recurses once per nesting level with no ceiling; a document of 100,000 nested arrays (200,000 bytes) crashed a probe with SIGSEGV instead of throwing JsonParseException, and with the default 8 MiB stack at -O0 about 13,400 levels (27 KB) are already enough.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Internal::ParseJson - documented to throw JsonParseException for malformed input; reached by every .cnj load, the .cnj compilers and the gamer-services offline achievement catalog
issues.expected: Parsing untrusted JSON either succeeds or throws JsonParseException. The parser's own class comment in {{src:modules/content/include/CNA/Internal/Json.hpp|Json.hpp}} promises "correct nesting/depth tracking". The XNB side, with the same threat model, bounds both type-name nesting and object-graph nesting (XnbReadLimits::maxObjectNestingDepth, 256, enforced by ContentReader::InnerReadObject).
issues.actual:
Detail::JsonParser::ParseValue dispatches { to ParseObject and [ to ParseArray, each of which calls ParseValue for every member or element. Nothing in Json.hpp counts depth, so stack use grows linearly with nesting and a deep document exhausts the thread's stack. That is a process crash, not an exception: no catch in ContentManager, the build tools or the gamer-services catalog reader can intercept it.

The parser is reached from ParseCnjEnvelope ({{src:modules/content/include/CNA/Internal/CnjEnvelope.hpp|CnjEnvelope.hpp}}), which every loose .cnj reader calls, directly from the typed loose readers in the per-type loader files of {{tree:modules/content/src/Xna|the content module}} ({{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentTexture2DLoaders.cpp|ContentTexture2DLoaders.cpp}}, {{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentModelLoaders.cpp|ContentModelLoaders.cpp}} and their siblings, which then hand the parsed tree to the shared readers of {{src:modules/content/include/CNA/Internal/CnjCanonicalRead.hpp|CnjCanonicalRead.hpp}}), the .cnj→.cnb compilers ({{src:modules/content/src/Cnb/CnjToCnb.cpp|CnjToCnb.cpp}}, {{src:modules/content/src/Cnb/CnbModelFromCnj.cpp|CnbModelFromCnj.cpp}}), the content pipeline's project, manifest and model stages, {{src:tools/content/content.cpp|tools/content/content.cpp}}, and ParseOfflineCatalog in {{src:modules/gamer-services/src/Internal/LocalGamerServicesStore.cpp|LocalGamerServicesStore.cpp}} (the title's offline achievement catalog). The store's own persisted files are parsed with nlohmann::json since GS-AUDIT-005 (38287637d) and no longer reach this parser.

sources.note: Detail::JsonParser::ParseValue / ParseObject / ParseArray - unbounded mutual recursion
ParseCnjEnvelope - calls ParseJson for every .cnj load
ParseOfflineCatalog - the offline achievement catalog is parsed with ParseJson; persisted store files use nlohmann::json (GS-AUDIT-005)
InnerReadObject - the XNB-side ObjectDepthGuard for comparison

issues.evidence:
Read at 3b43bd86. Executed at 009d40f5: a focused probe that includes only the header-only Json.hpp (it depends on the standard library alone), compiled with g++ 14.2 -std=c++23 at -O0 and -O2 and run on Linux x86-64 with the default 8 MiB main-thread stack. 1,000 and 10,000 nesting levels parse; 50,000 levels (at -O2) and 100,000 levels (both builds) end in SIGSEGV. A thread with a smaller stack fails sooner. The full ContentManager path was not executed; that every .cnj load reaches ParseJson is by reading ParseCnjEnvelope. There is no JSON or .cnj fuzz target: the fuzz suites under {{tree:modules/content/tests|modules/content/tests}} cover XNB containers, LZX, XNB writer input and CNB containers.

Independent re-verification: Reproduced by the audit at 009d40f5. A probe that includes only the header-only Json.hpp, compiled with g++ -std=c++23 at -O0 and run on Linux x86-64 with the default 8 MiB stack, parsed 10,000 and 13,281 nested-array levels and crashed with SIGSEGV from 13,437 levels (about 27 KB) up, with 20,000, 50,000 and 100,000 levels all crashing; no JsonParseException was thrown. The entry's earlier run also crashed at 100,000 levels at -O2 and parsed 10,000. The full ContentManager path was not executed; that every .cnj load reaches ParseJson is by reading ParseCnjEnvelope. There is no JSON or .cnj fuzz target.
issues.reproduction:
Compiled and run as described under Evidence (header-only; needs no other CNA code).

#include "CNA/Internal/Json.hpp"
#include <string>

int main()
{
    const std::size_t depth = 100000;                 // a 200,000-byte document
    const std::string doc = std::string(depth, '[') + std::string(depth, ']');
    try { (void)CNA::Internal::ParseJson(doc); }
    catch (const CNA::Internal::JsonParseException&) { return 0; } // wanted: rejected cleanly
    return 1;
}
// Observed at 009d40f5: SIGSEGV before either return.
issues.tests_current: {{src:modules/content/tests/CNA/Internal/JsonTests.cpp|JsonTests.cpp}} covers grammar, escapes, numbers and shallow nesting (ParsesNestedObjectsAndArrays); no case exceeds a few levels and none asserts a depth limit.
issues.regression_test: Two JsonTests cases around the chosen ceiling: a document nested exactly to the limit parses, one level deeper throws JsonParseException (run it on a deliberately small-stack thread so a missing check fails loudly). Plus one Load<T> test with a deeply nested .cnj expecting ContentLoadException, and ideally a .cnj case in the existing fuzz harness family.
issues.blast_radius: Any process that parses a .cnj or JSON file it did not write: games loading loose .cnj content (models, fonts, effects, animation clips, custom RegisterCnjLoader types), the cna-content build tool and pipeline, and the gamer-services offline achievement catalog (a title-shipped file). .xnb and .cnb content does not go through this parser.
issues.workaround: Load only trusted .cnj files at run time, or ship compiled .cnb content instead of loose .cnj.

issues.title: XnbReadLimits::maxFileSize is not applied to ContentManager's whole-file .xnb reads
issues.summary: The 64 MiB maxFileSize ceiling is enforced by the decompressors and the build-time canonical read, but ContentManager reads a run-time .xnb of up to INT32_MAX bytes and the manifest scan reads any size.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Internal::Xnb::XnbReadLimits::maxFileSize ("Largest .xnb file this reader will attempt to open, in bytes") as applied by ContentManager::Load
issues.expected: An .xnb larger than maxFileSize (64 MiB by default) is refused with ContentLoadException before its bytes are read into memory, as the field's documentation in {{src:modules/content/include/CNA/Internal/Xnb/XnbReadLimits.hpp|XnbReadLimits.hpp}} says and as CnbDocument::Parse does for CnbReadLimits::maxFileSize.
issues.actual: ContentManager::TryReadAssetBytes ({{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp|ContentManager.cpp}}) reads the whole file after checking only that it fits in INT32_MAX; LoadXnbAsset<T>, LoadXnbAssetUntyped and ReadStreamToEnd (the ReadAsset<T> route) check the same bound or none. ScanXnbReaderNames, run by RefreshContentManifest, reads every .xnb in the content root into a std::string with no size check at all. The only consumers of maxFileSize are the compressed-payload checks in {{src:modules/content/src/Xnb/XnbDecompression.cpp|XnbDecompression.cpp}} (LZX and LZ4) and the build-time canonical source read (ReadFile in {{src:modules/content/src/Xnb/XnbCanonicalAsset.cpp|XnbCanonicalAsset.cpp}}). An uncompressed .xnb between 64 MiB and 2 GiB is therefore read in full, up to a ~2 GiB allocation, before any other validation runs. The comment in {{src:modules/content/include/CNA/Internal/Xnb/XnbTypeReaderTable.hpp|XnbTypeReaderTable.hpp}} relies on a "coarse whole-stream limit (up to limits.maxFileSize)" that the run-time path does not have.

sources.note: ContentManager::TryReadAssetBytes, ReadStreamToEnd and ScanXnbReaderNames - whole-file reads
ContentManager::LoadXnbAsset - INT32_MAX check only
XnbReadLimits::maxFileSize
DecompressXnbPayload / DecompressXnbLz4Payload - the run-time consumers

issues.evidence: Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; not executed. The site's content-runtime internals page already records this ("an uncompressed .xnb between 64 MiB and 2 GiB is not refused by the file-size limit at run time"). The CNB path is not affected: CnbDocument::Parse checks its 512 MiB limit.
issues.tests_current: No test drives an .xnb above 64 MiB through ContentManager. {{src:modules/content/tests/CNA/Internal/Xnb/Lz4DecoderTests.cpp|Lz4DecoderTests.cpp}} exercises maxFileSize only on the decompressor; {{src:modules/content/tests/CNA/Content/Cnb/CnbSpecConformanceTests.cpp|CnbSpecConformanceTests.cpp}} pins the separate CNB limit.
issues.regression_test: Create a sparse file just over 64 MiB with a valid uncompressed XNB header (std::filesystem::resize_file keeps it cheap) and require Load<T> to throw ContentLoadException naming the size limit, without reading the body. A second case for GetContentManifest() should leave that entry's reader list empty without reading the file.
issues.blast_radius: The .xnb tier of Load<T>, ReadAsset<T> through the base OpenStream, untyped external references, and the content manifest scan. Compressed .xnb payloads and all .cnb files are bounded as documented.

issues.title: ReflectiveTypeReader has no TypeVersion, so an XNA .xnb for a [ContentSerializerTypeVersion] type is rejected
issues.summary: Reader versions must match exactly, as in XNA, but a reflective reader always reports version 0 and ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder cannot declare the version XNA's ReflectiveReader takes from the attribute.
issues.public_contract: ReflectiveTypeReader and ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder (ContentTypeReaderBase::getTypeVersionProperty / SupportsVersion); XNA 4.0 ReflectiveReader.TypeVersion
issues.expected: XNA 4.0's ContentTypeReaderManager.ReadTypeManifest rejects a type-reader table entry whose version differs from the reader's TypeVersion, and ReflectiveReader<T>.TypeVersion is the value of the type's [ContentSerializerTypeVersion] attribute, which XNA's automatic writer records beside the reader name (CNA's own {{src:modules/content/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ContentSerializerTypeVersionAttribute.hpp|ContentSerializerTypeVersionAttribute.hpp}} says the same). A CNA port that declares the reflective reader for such a type should load assets built with that version.
issues.actual:
ContentReader::InitializeTypeReaders ({{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentReader.cpp|ContentReader.cpp}}) calls SupportsVersion(entry.version), which by default is an exact match against getTypeVersionProperty(), which by default is 0 ({{src:modules/content/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ContentTypeReader.hpp|ContentTypeReader.hpp}}). ReflectiveTypeReader<T>, ReflectiveSharedTypeReader, AbstractReflectiveTypeReader and EnumTypeReader override neither, and ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder<T> ({{src:modules/content/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ReflectiveTypeReader.hpp|ReflectiveTypeReader.hpp}}, no version identifier anywhere in the file) has no way to set one. An XNA-built asset whose reflective entry carries version 2 fails with ContentLoadException "… at an unsupported version (2)".

The broader statement that every nonzero reader version is refused is true but, for the built-in readers, XNA-faithful: XNA's built-in readers are all version 0 and XNA enforces the same equality, so a nonzero version on a built-in reader name is not content XNA would load either. That part is not the defect.

sources.note: ContentReader::InitializeTypeReaders - SupportsVersion enforcement
ContentTypeReaderBase::SupportsVersion / getTypeVersionProperty defaults
ReflectiveTypeReader and ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder::Register - no version

issues.evidence: Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; not executed. Compared with the decompiled XNA 4.0 ContentTypeReaderManager.ReadTypeManifest and ReflectiveReader constructor. Hand-written readers can override getTypeVersionProperty() (the C API readers in {{src:modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiContentReaders.cpp|CnaCApiContentReaders.cpp}} and the content-pipeline compiler tests do), so the gap is confined to the reflective route. This entry narrows the original report's wording from "any nonzero version" to the reflective case by reading; no code changed.
issues.reproduction:
Illustrative; not compiled.

// XNA 4.0 game type, built by XNA's pipeline:
//   [ContentSerializerTypeVersion(2)] public class LevelData { public int Width; }
struct LevelData { int Width = 0; };

Content::ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder<LevelData>("MyGame.LevelData")
    .Field(&LevelData::Width)
    .Register();
LevelData level = content.Load<LevelData>("level1");
// throws ContentLoadException: "... at an unsupported version (2)"
issues.tests_current: {{src:modules/content/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ContentReaderTests.cpp|ContentReaderTests.cpp}} (ReaderVersionMismatchThrowsContentLoadException) pins the strict rule with a hand-written reader. No reflective-reader test uses a nonzero version.
issues.regression_test: Give ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder a way to declare the version (for example a TypeVersion(int) step), then a test that builds an in-memory XNB whose reflective entry says version 2, loads it with a builder declaring 2, and refuses it with a builder declaring 0.
issues.blast_radius: Only XNA content whose game types carry [ContentSerializerTypeVersion] and are loaded through the reflective builder. Built-in readers, hand-written ContentTypeReader<T> subclasses and unversioned reflective types are unaffected.
issues.workaround: Register a hand-written ContentTypeReader<T> (or a subclass of ReflectiveTypeReader<T>) that overrides getTypeVersionProperty(), with ContentTypeReaderManager::AddTypeCreator under the same canonical reader name, instead of calling the builder's Register() (the first registration for a name is the one that stays).

issues.title: PlaneIntersectionType's Doxygen swaps the meaning of Front and Back
issues.summary: PlaneIntersectionType.hpp documents Front as the negative half-space and Back as the positive one, the opposite of what every CNA classification returns and of XNA's meaning.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::PlaneIntersectionType (Front, Back) as documented in its public header
issues.expected: Front means the whole volume lies in the positive half-space, the side the plane normal points to (Dot(Normal, p) + D > 0); Back means the negative half-space. That is what XNA 4.0 returns: its Plane.Intersects(ref BoundingSphere, out PlaneIntersectionType) answers Front when the signed centre distance exceeds the radius (read from the IL of the genuine XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework assembly; not executed).
issues.actual: The comments in {{src:modules/math/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/PlaneIntersectionType.hpp|PlaneIntersectionType.hpp}} say Front is "in the negative half-space of the plane" and Back "in the positive half-space". Every implementation does the opposite: Plane::IntersectsPoint returns Front for a positive distance, BoundingSphere::Intersects(const Plane&, PlaneIntersectionType&) returns Front when the distance exceeds the radius, BoundingBox::Intersects(const Plane&, PlaneIntersectionType&) returns Front when even the box's most negative vertex is on the positive side, and BoundingFrustum::Intersects(const Plane&, PlaneIntersectionType&) builds on IntersectsPoint. The comment text is FNA's, which carries the same inverted wording. A reader who follows the header inverts a culling or classification test.

sources.note: the Front and Back Doxygen comments
Plane::IntersectsPoint: Front for distance > 0
BoundingSphere::Intersects(const Plane&, PlaneIntersectionType&)
BoundingBox::Intersects(const Plane&, PlaneIntersectionType&)
checks only distinctness and the XNA ordinals
validate_plane: a box below the ground plane is BACK, a sphere above it FRONT

issues.evidence: Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; nothing was built or executed for this entry. The contradiction is between the header text and four function bodies; the C ABI smoke test {{src:modules/c-api/tests/pure_c/GeometrySmoke.c|GeometrySmoke.c}} pins the implemented meaning (FRONT for a sphere above the plane y = 0 whose normal points up). XNA's meaning was read from its IL.
issues.reproduction:
Illustrative; not compiled or run for this entry.

Plane ground(Vector3(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f), 0.0f);                          // normal points up
PlaneIntersectionType t = ground.Intersects(BoundingSphere(Vector3(0.0f, 5.0f, 0.0f), 1.0f));
// t == PlaneIntersectionType::Front: the sphere is in the POSITIVE half-space,
// although the header comment on Front says "negative".
issues.tests_current: {{src:modules/math/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/PlaneIntersectionTypeTests.cpp|PlaneIntersectionTypeTests.cpp}} checks that the three values are distinct and have the XNA ordinals 0, 1 and 2. The implemented meaning is pinned by {{src:modules/c-api/tests/pure_c/GeometrySmoke.c|GeometrySmoke.c}} and by the plane cases of the bounding-volume suites; nothing checks documentation.
issues.regression_test: A documentation fix (swap the two comments to XNA's wording). The existing semantic tests already pin the behaviour; a one-line unit test named for the convention (a sphere on the normal's side is Front) would make the intent explicit.
issues.blast_radius: Documentation only: the public header, generated API documentation and IDE tooltips. No behaviour changes, and the C ABI enum identities (CNA_PLANE_INTERSECTION_*) are unaffected.
issues.workaround: Rely on the implementation: Front means entirely on the side the plane normal points to.

issues.title: Curve::ComputeTangent Smooth tangents test the key spacing against two different epsilons, where XNA tests the value difference against one
issues.summary: For CurveTangent::Smooth, ComputeTangent zeroes the in tangent when the neighbour span is below 2^-24 but the out tangent only below the smallest denormal, while XNA zeroes both when the neighbours' value difference is below FLT_EPSILON.
issues.public_contract: Curve::ComputeTangent(int, CurveTangent, CurveTangent), ComputeTangents (all overloads) with CurveTangent::Smooth; the C ABI cna_curve_compute_tangent* routes
issues.expected: XNA 4.0 (read from the IL of the genuine XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework assembly; not executed), for a Smooth key with neighbours (p0, v0) and (p1, v1): the in tangent is 0 when |v1 - v0| < 1.1920929E-07 (FLT_EPSILON), otherwise (v1 - v0) * |p0 - p| / (p1 - p0); the out tangent uses the same test and (v1 - v0) * |p1 - p| / (p1 - p0). Both tangents share one test on the value difference.
issues.actual:
• {{src:modules/math/src/Curve.cpp|Curve.cpp}} computes pn = p1 - p0 and tests the spacing, not the values, with two different thresholds:
  • in tangent: MathHelper::WithinEpsilon(pn, 0.0f), i.e. |pn| < MachineEpsilonFloat (2^-24, about 5.96e-8), else (v1 - v0) * ((p - p0) / pn);
  • out tangent: std::fabs(pn) < std::numeric_limits<float>::denorm_min() (about 1.4e-45, so in practice only pn == 0), else (v1 - v0) * ((p1 - p) / pn).
  • Consequences: neighbours whose values differ by less than FLT_EPSILON get a tiny non-zero tangent instead of XNA's 0; for a neighbour span between 1.4e-45 and 5.96e-8 the in tangent is zeroed while the out tangent is still computed, (v1 - v0) * (p1 - p) / pn, which for sorted keys is at most |v1 - v0| in size, so the two tangents of one key follow different rules and the in tangent loses the value XNA gives it; and because the operations are ordered differently, ordinary tangents may differ from XNA's in the last bit (not measured). CNA's form is FNA's (MathHelper.WithinEpsilon for in, float.Epsilon for out); the ratio between the two thresholds is about 4e37.

sources.note: Curve::ComputeTangent(int, CurveTangent, CurveTangent): the two Smooth branches
MathHelper::WithinEpsilon and GetMachineEpsilonFloat (2^-24)
CurveTest.ComputeTangentSmoothMiddleKey uses three equal values
the generated C ABI tangent routes call ComputeTangent and ComputeTangents

issues.evidence:
Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; the audit's own executed comparison follows below. Both thresholds and formulas are in the function body. The XNA algorithm was read from its IL; an earlier reading that treated the out-tangent test as the correct one compared against FNA only, and against XNA both branches deviate. Ordinary inputs do differ in the last bit; the executed comparison below measures how often.

Independent re-verification: Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; nothing was built or executed for this entry. Both thresholds and formulas are in the function body. The XNA algorithm was read from its IL; an earlier reading that treated the out-tangent test as the correct one compared against FNA only, and against XNA both branches deviate. The C ABI curve smoke test does run a Smooth out tangent (compute_tangents_in_out with Flat in and Smooth out over keys at 0, 1, 2 with values 0, 2, 4 expects 2.0), but that input has evenly spaced keys on which CNA and XNA agree, so it cannot tell the rules apart; the earlier statement that it exercises Linear tangents only is wrong. Whether ordinary inputs differ in the last bit was not measured.

Independent re-verification: Reproduced by the audit at 009d40f5. That commit's Curve.cpp was built with g++ -O0 and compared with a float32 model of the decompiled XNA 4.0 IL. The entry's reproduction gave CNA tangents of 5e-09 against XNA's 0. Keys at 0, 1e-9 and 2e-9 with values 0, 3 and 6 gave CNA in=0 and out=3 against XNA's 3 and 3. On 1,000,000 random sorted key triples CNA's tangents differed from the model's in about 34% of cases, by at most 2 ulp, because the operations are ordered differently (real XNA on an x87 JIT may keep wider intermediates, so the last-bit figure is against a strict float32 model). The XNA algorithm was read from its IL; an earlier reading that treated the out-tangent test as the correct one compared against FNA only, and against XNA both branches deviate. The C ABI curve smoke test does run a Smooth out tangent (compute_tangents_in_out with Flat in and Smooth out over keys at 0, 1, 2 with values 0, 2, 4 expects 2.0), but that input has evenly spaced keys on which CNA and XNA agree, so it cannot tell the rules apart.

Illustrative; the audit's executed probe is described under Evidence.

c.getKeysProperty().Add(CurveKey(0.0f, 0.0f));
c.getKeysProperty().Add(CurveKey(1.0f, 0.0f));
c.getKeysProperty().Add(CurveKey(2.0f, 1.0e-8f));   // neighbour values differ by less than FLT_EPSILON
c.ComputeTangent(1, CurveTangent::Smooth);

The C ABI curve smoke test runs one Smooth out tangent (Flat in, Smooth out, keys at 0, 1 and 2 with values 0, 2 and 4, expecting 2.0), but on evenly spaced keys, where CNA and XNA agree, so it cannot tell the rules apart. issues.regression_test: Smooth tangents for unequally spaced keys with unequal values (for example positions 0, 1, 3 and values 0, 1, 5, expecting 5/3 and 10/3), for neighbour values closer than FLT_EPSILON (expecting 0 for both), and for a neighbour span below 2^-24; ideally the expected values come from running the genuine XNA runtime through CNA's existing framework-oracle tooling.
issues.blast_radius: Curves whose tangents are computed at run time with CurveTangent::Smooth (directly or through the C ABI). Curves loaded from content keep the tangents stored in the file and are unaffected unless the game recomputes them.
issues.workaround: Set the tangents explicitly with CurveKey::setTangentInProperty and setTangentOutProperty instead of computing Smooth tangents.

issues.title: A copied Texture2D or TextureCube raises GraphicsDevice.ResourceDestroyed without a matching ResourceCreated, and a copy taken after its device died still reaches the device on disposal
issues.summary: Texture copies are now registered with their device, but a copy never raises ResourceCreated while its disposal raises ResourceDestroyed, and a copy taken after the device was destroyed still touches the dead device's texture slots on disposal.
issues.public_contract: GraphicsDevice.ResourceCreated / GraphicsDevice.ResourceDestroyed; Texture2D(const Texture2D&), TextureCube(const TextureCube&); GraphicsResource copy constructor; Texture::Dispose(bool)
issues.expected: Every wrapper a device tracks should produce a balanced event stream: a listener that counts ResourceCreated and ResourceDestroyed (a leak tracker, the Inspector, a game's own resource census) should see one destroy per create. And disposing a texture wrapper must never touch a GraphicsDevice that no longer exists: GraphicsDevice::AddResourceReference is documented as the registration that lets the device “dispose registered resources before its own renderer is destroyed, preventing use-after-free”.
issues.actual:
• Fixed since the finding was first recorded: moves (TransferResourceReference, TransferMovedTexture, gated on the weak graphicsDeviceLifetime_ token) and, since MSR-027 (af3c5037c), copies. Texture2D and TextureCube now define their copy constructor and copy assignment ({{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/Texture2D.cpp|Texture2D.cpp}}, {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/TextureCube.cpp|TextureCube.cpp}}): a copy calls AddResourceReference on a live device, and a copy assignment across devices removes the wrapper from the old device's registry and adds it to the new one, so GraphicsDevice::Dispose() marks every live copy disposed and a ContentManager cache hit is tracked.
  • Still present: events. GraphicsResource(const GraphicsResource&) ({{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsResource.cpp|GraphicsResource.cpp}}) raises no ResourceCreated, and the texture copy constructors only call AddResourceReference, but GraphicsResource::Dispose(bool) calls OnResourceDestroyed for every registered wrapper whose device is alive. Every texture copy (each ContentManager::Load<Texture2D> cache hit returns one) therefore adds a ResourceDestroyed with no matching ResourceCreated.
  • Still present: copies made after the device died. When the source's device lifetime token has expired, the copy constructor skips registration but GraphicsResource(const&) still sets isDisposed_ to false and keeps the raw graphicsDevice_ pointer. When that copy is disposed, Texture::Dispose ({{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/Texture.cpp|Texture.cpp}}) calls RemoveDisposedTexture on graphicsDevice_->getTexturesProperty() and getVertexTexturesProperty() without checking the lifetime token, so it reads the storage of a destroyed GraphicsDevice. This needs a copy taken from a wrapper whose device is already gone, for example a ContentManager cache hit after the device was disposed and destroyed.

sources.note: GraphicsResource copy constructor raises no ResourceCreated; Dispose(bool) raises ResourceDestroyed for a registered wrapper on a live device
Texture2D copy constructor and copy assignment (MSR-027): register the copy, move the registration across devices; skip registration when the device lifetime has expired
TextureCube copy constructor and copy assignment (MSR-027), same rules
Texture::Dispose: RemoveDisposedTexture on the device's texture collections without a lifetime check
AddResourceReference, OnResourceCreated, OnResourceDestroyed, Dispose(bool) drains resources_
Load: the cache stores a copy and every cache hit returns another copy through std::any_cast

issues.evidence:
Checked by reading {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsResource.cpp|GraphicsResource.cpp}}, {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}}, {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/Texture2D.cpp|Texture2D.cpp}}, {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/TextureCube.cpp|TextureCube.cpp}}, {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/Texture.cpp|Texture.cpp}} and {{src:modules/content/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ContentManager.hpp|ContentManager.hpp}} at 3b43bd86. Not executed: a focused run needs a GraphicsDevice with a real renderer, which is outside a pure-source probe.

Independently observed as a separate finding (merged): The GraphicsResource copy constructor neither registers the copy nor raises ResourceCreated, but Dispose(bool) (also run from the destructor) raises ResourceDestroyed for any live device, so every short-lived copy produces an unmatched destroy event.

Re-verified at c1c316b9: MSR-027 (af3c5037c) fixed the tracking half of this entry (the copy registration, cross-device copy assignment and device disposal of copies), pinned by GraphicsResourceTest.CopiedTexturesAreTrackedAndCanOutliveOwningDevice and GraphicsResourceTest.CopyAssignedTexturesTransferDeviceTracking; the event imbalance and the unchecked device access in Texture::Dispose survive, by reading; not executed.
issues.reproduction:
Illustrative, not compiled:

GraphicsDevice device;
int created = 0, destroyed = 0;
device.ResourceCreated += [&](auto*, const auto&) { ++created; };
device.ResourceDestroyed += [&](auto*, const auto&) { ++destroyed; };
{
    Texture2D original(device, 4, 4);   // created == 1
    Texture2D copy(original);           // registered, but created stays 1
}                                       // destroyed == 2: one unmatched destroy
issues.tests_current: {{src:modules/graphics/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/GraphicsResourceDisplayModeCollectionTests.cpp|GraphicsResourceDisplayModeCollectionTests.cpp}} pins the tracking: CopiedTexturesAreTrackedAndCanOutliveOwningDevice (a copy raises GetTrackedResourceCount(), is disposed with its device and can be destroyed afterwards), CopyAssignedTexturesTransferDeviceTracking (copy assignment across two devices) and CrossDeviceMoveAssignmentTransfersTrackingAndDetachesOldBindings. No test counts ResourceCreated against ResourceDestroyed for a copied texture, and none copies a texture after its device was destroyed.
issues.regression_test: Add to GraphicsResourceTest: (1) subscribe to both device events, copy a device-created Texture2D and a TextureCube, destroy everything and require equal create and destroy counts; (2) destroy a device, then copy a texture that outlived it and destroy the copy, run under AddressSanitizer.
issues.blast_radius: Affected: listeners of GraphicsDevice.ResourceCreated/ResourceDestroyed that pair the two events (resource counters, leak reports), which over-count destroys whenever textures are copied, in particular for every ContentManager cache hit; and code that copies a texture wrapper after its device was destroyed (statics or caches that outlive the Game). Not affected: device tracking and disposal of copies, moves, move-only resources (VertexBuffer, IndexBuffer, RenderTarget2D, Texture3D) and the state objects, whose copies share one identity.
issues.workaround: Do not pair ResourceCreated and ResourceDestroyed counts for textures; use GetTrackedResourceCount() instead. Keep texture wrappers and content caches inside the lifetime of the Game, so no copy is taken after the device is gone.

issues.title: devices-tests.yml's exact-name gtest filters skip nine Microsoft::Devices suites and never match the FileDialog and MessageBox suites
issues.summary: DEVICES_GTEST_FILTER misses 34 of 479 TEST definitions under modules/devices/tests, and CNA_DEVICES_GTEST_FILTER names FileDialogTests.* and MessageBoxTests.*, which match no suite, so the 12 FileDialog and MessageBox cases run in no CI job.

issues.expected: The workflow is the only CI job that builds CnaTests with CNA_DEVICES=ON and a sanitizer (the devices-ubsan preset). Its first filter is documented in the workflow as selecting "every TEST(...) under modules/devices/tests/Microsoft/Devices/, no more and no fewer", kept in step with {{src:docs/devices-build.md|docs/devices-build.md}}. Its second filter was added precisely so the CNA::Devices extension suites - FileDialog, MessageBox, Clipboard, SystemTray and the rest - run in CI at all, because the job "silently never compiled that surface" before.
issues.actual:
Matching both filter strings against the TEST/TEST_F definitions at TARGET with gtest's rules (a pattern Suite.* matches that exact suite name only):

  • DEVICES_GTEST_FILTER names 21 suites and selects 445 of the 479 definitions under {{tree:modules/devices/tests/Microsoft/Devices|modules/devices/tests/Microsoft/Devices}}. Nine suites are missing: DevicesShutdownCoordinatorTest (4), DevicesShutdownOrderingTest (3), EnvironmentTests (3), IndependentReferenceCrossCheckTests (2), KeyboardAccelerometerTest (4, added by INPUT-EMU-001), NativeDiagnosticSinkTest (9), PlatformSensorMigrationTests (4), PlatformVibrateMigrationTests (4) and SensorHeaderMacroHygiene (1, added on 2026-10-24 by ec2d8b692). They are compiled into CnaTests everywhere and run unsanitized in general-tests-ci.yml, but never under this job's UBSan build.
  • CNA_DEVICES_GTEST_FILTER lists FileDialogTests.* and MessageBoxTests.*. Since the PLAT-90a refactor (commit 234b6d3e3) the files define the fixtures FileDialogTest and MessageBoxTest plus FileDialogWithoutAServiceTest and MessageBoxWithoutAServiceTest, so neither pattern matches anything and gtest runs the other eight suites without complaint. The dialog tests are wrapped in #ifdef CNA_DEVICES, CNA_DEVICES defaults to OFF, and no other workflow turns it on, so these 12 cases run in no CI job.

The workflow header also still says every CNA::Devices test drives an injected backend through SetBackendForTesting(), the seam PLAT-90a removed in favour of a canned dialog platform.

issues.title: run-all-renderer-smoke-tests.sh ignores the build's exit status, and its '-- -k' build flag aborts every Ninja build, so smoke verdicts can come from stale binaries
issues.summary: The orchestrator runs cmake --build <dir> -j4 -- -k and discards the result; -k without a count is a make option that Ninja rejects, so in a Ninja tree nothing is rebuilt and ctest runs whatever executables the tree already holds.
issues.public_contract: scripts/run-all-renderer-smoke-tests.sh (default, --tier and --multi modes): a renderer that configures and builds but fails its smoke test fails the run
issues.expected: The script's header says a renderer "that DOES configure/build but whose smoke test fails makes the overall run fail", so that it "composes cleanly as a CI step", and {{src:docs/runtime-renderer-selection.md|docs/runtime-renderer-selection.md}} recommends its --multi "HEADLESS;SOFTWARE;STUB" mode. A verdict only means something if the smoke tests run against binaries built from the current tree, and a build that did not happen must not be reported as a pass.
issues.actual:
Both modes build with cmake --build "${dir}" -j4 -- -k and never read the exit status (the comment explains -k as a way past an unrelated demo build error; "ctest is the real signal"). CMake appends the arguments after -- to the native tool unchanged. GNU make reads -k as keep-going; Ninja's -k takes a count, so ninja -j 4 -k stops with "option requires an argument -- 'k'" before building anything. The script configures a missing tree with CMake's default generator, but it reuses existing trees whatever their generator, and the --multi tree, cmake-build-multi, is exactly the binaryDir of the multi-renderer preset in {{src:CMakePresets.json|CMakePresets.json}}, which inherits base-ninja and names the same HEADLESS;SOFTWARE;STUB set.

ctest then runs regardless. A smoke executable that was never built is reported Not Run, so the renderer shows FAIL with a misleading cause; one left from an earlier build runs the old code, so the renderer can show PASS for a tree that did not build. Under make the same happens to a smoke target whose own compile fails, since -k leaves the previous executable in place.

sources.note: the build step of the --multi branch and of the per-renderer loop: cmake --build ... -j4 -- -k, exit status unused
multi-renderer preset: binaryDir cmake-build-multi, inherits base-ninja

issues.evidence: Read at 3b43bd86, where the per-renderer table names cmake-build-debug, cmake-build-sdlgpu and cmake-build-webgpu. Executed at 009d40f5: only Ninja's argument parsing, with Ninja 1.12.1 on the review host (ninja -k with no count prints "option requires an argument -- 'k'" and its usage text). The script was not run and no CNA tree was configured. What changed since this was first reported, and is not part of this entry: the renderer set is no longer a fixed four-identity list (--tier routine|full, where full covers every family that registers a GraphicsSmoke test), the multi-renderer mode was added, its label lookup refuses to count "no matching test" as a pass, and a configure failure is deliberately reported as SKIPPED ("not available on this machine"), which is the script's stated contract. No workflow calls the script; it is a manual maintainer tool.

Illustrative; not run for this entry.

cmake --preset multi-renderer        # Ninja tree in cmake-build-multi
scripts/run-all-renderer-smoke-tests.sh --multi "HEADLESS;SOFTWARE;STUB"
# build step: ninja: option requires an argument -- 'k'
# the script continues and reports per-renderer results from whatever the tree contains
issues.tests_current: None: the script has no self-test and no workflow invokes it. multi-renderer-ci.yml builds and tests the same HEADLESS;SOFTWARE;STUB set with its own steps and does check its build.
issues.regression_test: Treat a failed build as a result (record the renderer as FAIL (build) and skip its ctest, or exit non-zero), and pass keep-going in the generator's own spelling (-k for make, -k 0 for Ninja) or drop it. A small shell test can point the script at a tree whose build is made to fail and assert a non-zero exit.
issues.blast_radius: Local renderer smoke runs by maintainers, in every mode (existing cmake-build-debug, cmake-build-sdlgpu, cmake-build-webgpu trees that happen to be Ninja trees, --tier, and --multi). CI and shipped code are unaffected.

issues.title: A relative ContentManager root still follows the working directory on the non-SDL3 platforms, and the loose tier cannot see Android packaged assets
issues.summary: ContentManager now roots a relative RootDirectory under TitleLocation and reads .cnb through the platform on Android, but TitleLocation is the working directory on the non-SDL3 platforms and the loose tier still gates on std::filesystem::exists.
issues.public_contract: ContentManager::RootDirectory and ContentManager::Load path resolution (XNA resolves through TitleContainer.OpenStream, relative to the title location)
issues.expected: XNA 4.0's ContentManager.OpenStream combines RootDirectory with the asset name and opens it through TitleContainer.OpenStream, which resolves a relative path against the title location (the executable's directory), independent of the working directory. CNA's own TitleContainer::ResolveRealPath ({{src:modules/runtime/src/TitleContainer.cpp|TitleContainer.cpp}}) resolves through TitleLocation::getPathProperty(), which is the platform's GetBasePath(): on the SDL3 platform that is SDL_GetBasePath() ({{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3SystemServices.cpp|Sdl3SystemServices.cpp}}), the executable's directory, so there TitleContainer follows XNA's rule; CNA's {{src:docs/apple-platforms.md|docs/apple-platforms.md}} states that "Content is loaded relative to SDL_GetBasePath()". On Android every content tier should read the APK's packaged assets.
issues.actual:
BuildAssetPath joins TitleRootedDirectory() and the asset name. Off Android, that function passes the root through CNA::Internal::ResolveContentRoot ({{src:modules/content/src/Internal/ContentRoot.cpp|ContentRoot.cpp}}): a relative root is used under the title path (TitleLocation's path, else the platform's GetBasePath()) when that directory exists, and is otherwise left relative to the working directory. On the SDL3 platform the title path is the executable directory. On the headless and terminal platforms it is the working directory, because StandardFileSystem::GetBasePath ({{src:modules/platform/src/Common/StandardFileSystem.cpp|StandardFileSystem.cpp}}) returns current_path(). A game started from another directory therefore still misses its default Content root there.

On Android the root is used as given, and TryReadAssetBytes forwards a relative path to the platform file system. That reaches packaged assets for the .xnb tier and, since BL-19, for both .cnb tiers. ResolveAssetPath ({{src:modules/content/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/ContentManager.hpp|ContentManager.hpp}}) still tests the literal path, the .cnj candidate and every reader extension with std::filesystem::exists, which cannot see APK assets, and the built-in Texture2D loose reader opens through ImageLoader::Load's std::ifstream.

Fixed since first recorded: a relative root resolves under the title (CBIND-140, 9976f4909) and the .cnb tiers read through TryReadAssetBytes (BL-19, 5d275f556). Earlier fixes: TitleContainer and TitleLocation have in-tree consumers ({{src:modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiGameProperties.cpp|CnaCApiGameProperties.cpp}}), and the .xnb tier's Android route goes through Sdl3FileSystem::TryLoadFileIgnoringCase.

TitleLocation::DetectBasePath
ImageLoader::Load - reads through std::ifstream

issues.title: StorageContainer::GetFileNames/GetDirectoryNames(searchPattern): GlobMatch treats ? as one byte and compares case-sensitively on every host
issues.summary: The hand-written matcher behind the pattern overloads matches ? against one UTF-8 byte rather than one character and compares bytes case-sensitively even on Windows, where XNA's Directory.GetFiles matching is not; only star patterns over ASCII names are exercised by any test, and only through the C ABI smoke test.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Storage::StorageContainer::GetFileNames(const std::string& searchPattern) and GetDirectoryNames(const std::string& searchPattern); the C name-count and name-copy routes that take a search_pattern
issues.expected: XNA documents the pattern overloads with "Both single-character ("?") and multicharacter ("*") wildcards are supported" (xna4-spec StorageContainer) and implements them with Directory.GetFiles/GetDirectories (decompiled StorageContainer), which match UTF-16 characters and follow the file system's case rules, case-insensitive on Windows. CNA's header describes the argument only as a "Glob pattern". A game that lists save slots with "slot?.sav" expects the same result on every host.
issues.actual: GlobMatch is a 22-line backtracking matcher in an anonymous namespace of {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp|StorageContainer.cpp}}; its own comment says '?' = any single char. It compares bytes of the UTF-8 file name: ? consumes exactly one byte, so a non-ASCII character (two to four bytes) needs as many ?; every other byte, the dot included, matches only itself, case-sensitively on every host. "?.sav" therefore misses é.sav, and "slot?.sav" misses SLOT1.SAV on Windows, where the file system treats the two spellings as one name and XNA would return it. No C++ storage test calls either pattern overload. The only test that does is the C ABI smoke test ({{src:modules/c-api/tests/pure_c/StorageSmoke.c|StorageSmoke.c}}, registered as CApi_StorageSmoke only when CNA_BUILD_C_API is ON; it is OFF by default and no workflow at TARGET enables it), which checks the star patterns lev*, z*, *.dat and *.png against ASCII names. The ? wildcard, non-ASCII names and case are not tested anywhere.

The storage guide already documents the byte semantics for game authors; nothing tests them.

issues.title: Guide message-box and keyboard-input results expose an AsyncWaitHandle that is already signalled while the answer is pending
issues.summary: Guide's message-box and keyboard-input results construct their AsyncWaitHandle already signalled, so WaitOne returns while IsCompleted is still false; End* now waits by running the game's modal frames and refuses only when no running game shows the Guide.
issues.public_contract: getAsyncWaitHandleProperty() and getIsCompletedProperty() of the IAsyncResult returned by Guide::BeginShowMessageBox and Guide::BeginShowKeyboardInput; EndShowMessageBox and EndShowKeyboardInput
issues.expected: The IAsyncResult contract: AsyncWaitHandle is signalled when the operation completes, so waiting on it and then calling End* yields the result. XNA's GamerServicesDispatcher.Update advances pending gamer-services work, and the synchronous-wrapper pattern CNA inherited from FNA (while (!result->IsCompleted) UpdateAsync();) relies on something advancing it.
issues.actual: {{src:modules/gamer-services/src/Xna/GuideDialogs.cpp|GuideDialogs.cpp}}'s GuideAction, the base of the message-box and keyboard-input results, constructs its EventWaitHandle signalled (asyncWaitHandle_(true, ManualReset)), and nothing resets it, so WaitOne() returns at once while IsCompleted is still false. End* no longer throws while the answer is pending: since 70d6f109e it claims the result and runs the game's modal frames until the Guide is answered, and it throws InvalidOperationException only when no running game presents the Guide. GamerServicesDispatcher::Update now pumps service work, but the answer comes only from the Guide drawn in the game's frames, so a thread that waits on the handle and then calls End* still blocks in End*, or gets the exception, and a game-thread loop that pumps GamerServicesDispatcher::UpdateAsync() until IsCompleted never ends.

issues.title: SongTypeReader and MediaLibraryIndex offer song formats (.opus, .aac, .wma) that no CNA-configured mixer decodes
issues.summary: Load<Song> resolves .opus, .aac and .wma files and the media library indexes .opus, but neither the vendored SDL3_mixer build nor CNA's ALSA mixer decodes them, so such songs load and then silently fail to play.
issues.public_contract: ContentManager::Load<Media::Song> (loose-file tier, SongTypeReader::GetExtensions) and MediaLibrary::getSongsProperty (MediaLibraryIndex scan)
issues.expected: A loose-file extension list and a library scan should offer only formats the build can play. {{src:modules/media/src/Internal/MediaLibraryIndex.cpp|MediaLibraryIndex.cpp}} states that rule for itself (“Only formats this project's selected mixer decoder can genuinely PLAY are indexed”) and leaves out .m4a/.aac for exactly that reason. XNA's contract for Load<T> is a usable asset or a ContentLoadException, so a format the build cannot decode should either not be resolved or be refused at load time.
issues.actual:
SongTypeReader::GetExtensions in {{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentMediaLoaders.cpp|ContentMediaLoaders.cpp}} returns .mp3 .ogg .wav .flac .opus .aac .wma, and SongTypeReader::Read constructs Media::Song(path, stem), which only checks that the file exists. What can actually be decoded:

  • SDL3 audio (the default): {{src:cmake/ThirdPartySDL.cmake|ThirdPartySDL.cmake}} builds the vendored SDL3_mixer (pinned at 3075d3ed, version 3.3.0) with SDLMIXER_OPUS=OFF and the mpg123, vorbisfile, tremor, WavPack, libFLAC, GME, libxmp and FluidSynth back ends off, which leaves dr_mp3, stb_vorbis, dr_flac, WAV/AIFF/VOC/AU and Timidity. SDL3_mixer has no AAC or WMA decoder in any configuration.
  • ALSA audio: DecodeMixerAudio in {{src:modules/audio/src/Backend/CnaMixer/CnaMixerDecoders.cpp|CnaMixerDecoders.cpp}} plays WAV, Ogg Vorbis, MP3 and FLAC and refuses Ogg Opus by name.

So a song whose only file is theme.opus, theme.aac or theme.wma loads successfully; MediaPlayer::Play then reaches PlaySong, LoadMixerAudioFile returns nothing, and PlaySong returns without an error (the consequences are described in the entry on MediaPlayer::Play's failure handling). The resolution order puts these three after .mp3, .ogg, .wav and .flac, so a playable sibling of the same name wins.

The media library repeats the mismatch: HasSupportedAudioExtension indexes .opus and names “decoder_opus (.opus)” as part of the bundled decoder set, which the vendored build disables, and the class comment in {{src:modules/media/include/CNA/Internal/Media/MediaLibraryIndex.hpp|MediaLibraryIndex.hpp}} still lists only .ogg/.oga/.mp3/.wav while the scan indexes six extensions. With CNA_USE_SYSTEM_SDL=ON the host's SDL3_mixer is linked instead and may include Opus; .aac and .wma stay undecodable.

issues.title: HEADLESS reports occlusion-query support and a precise pixel count while its query always answers 1
issues.summary: HEADLESS inherits OcclusionQuery = true and the default isPixelCountPreciseEXT() = true, but HeadlessOcclusionQueryRenderer completes at once and returns PixelCount() == 1 whatever was drawn.
issues.public_contract: CNA::GraphicsCapability::OcclusionQuery and OcclusionQuery::isPixelCountPreciseEXT() on the HEADLESS renderer
issues.expected: GraphicsCapability::OcclusionQuery is documented as "Real raster-sample occlusion queries (OcclusionQuery.Begin/End/PixelCount)", and the comment on IGraphicsRenderer::SupportsCapability requires every renderer with a narrower contract, "including no-renderer" ones, to override the applicable entries truthfully. OcclusionQuery::isPixelCountPreciseEXT() (CNAEXT) is true only "when the pixel count is a genuine per-fragment tally".
issues.actual: HeadlessRenderer::SupportsCapability overrides only Texture3D, AdditiveBlending and MultiStreamVertexInput; OcclusionQuery reaches default: return true. HeadlessRenderer::CreateOcclusionQuery returns a HeadlessOcclusionQueryRenderer whose End() marks it complete and whose PixelCount() is the constant 1 (its comment calls this the conservative "everything visible" answer). It does not override the renderer-side PixelCountIsPreciseEXT(), which OcclusionQuery::isPixelCountPreciseEXT() forwards, so the interface default true is reported. On a HiDef HEADLESS device a game sees occlusion queries advertised, a result available at once, PixelCount == 1 for any geometry (including none), and a claim that 1 is an exact fragment tally.

issues.title: Curve::Evaluate divides by a zero key span in the cyclic loop modes and converts the resulting infinity to int
issues.summary: When every key shares one position, GetNumberOfCycle divides by the zero key span without a guard and casts the infinity to int (undefined behaviour) in the Cycle, CycleOffset and Oscillate loop modes, where XNA's cycle count is 0.
issues.public_contract: Curve::Evaluate(float) for curves whose keys all share one position, with a Cycle, CycleOffset or Oscillate pre- or post-loop; C ABI cna_curve_evaluate
issues.expected: XNA 4.0 guards the division (read from the IL of the genuine XNA 4.0 Microsoft.Xna.Framework assembly; not executed): CurveKeyCollection.ComputeCacheValues leaves the inverse time range at 0 unless the range is above float.Epsilon (1.401298E-45), so the cycle count of an all-coincident curve is 0 and XNA returns finite values from its keys.
issues.actual:
• CurveKeyCollection::Add in {{src:modules/math/src/CurveKeyCollection.cpp|CurveKeyCollection.cpp}} accepts a key at an existing position (it is inserted after the equal ones), as XNA's collection does.
  • All keys at one position p with a Cycle, CycleOffset or Oscillate pre- or post-loop: GetNumberOfCycle in {{src:modules/math/src/Curve.cpp|Curve.cpp}} computes (position - p) / 0, an infinity, and static_cast<int> of it is undefined behaviour in C++ (typically INT_MIN on x86-64). A CycleOffset loop then adds cycle * (last.Value - first.Value), so a curve whose key values differ returns a huge number; XNA returns a finite value from the keys.
  • The path is ported unchanged from FNA's C# implementation (read at FNA commit 1358793, 2026-08-01).

issues.title: BoundingFrustum::Intersects(Plane) counts a corner lying on the plane as Intersecting, where XNA 4.0 answers Back
issues.summary: The Plane overload treats a corner at zero distance as Intersecting, so a frustum touching a plane from behind is Intersecting where XNA (distance > 0 is Front, everything else Back) answers Back. The box and sphere overloads now match XNA.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::BoundingFrustum::Intersects(Plane) and its out-parameter overload
issues.expected: XNA 4.0 (IL): BoundingFrustum.Intersects(ref Plane) classifies each corner with dot + D > 0 as Front and everything else (including exactly 0) as Back.

issues.title: Game::PollEvents fires the renderer's test-only context-loss hooks on F9/F10 in every build
issues.summary: A non-repeated F9 or F10 press in any CNA game calls the renderer's DebugSimulateContextLoss() or DebugRestoreContext(), a channel CNA itself describes as a test seam, with no build, option or opt-out guard.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Game::Run() / Tick() (through the private PollEvents); CNA::Internal::Renderers::IGraphicsRenderer::DebugSimulateContextLoss() and DebugRestoreContext()
issues.expected: XNA's Game reserves no keys: a key press only reaches the game's input state. CNA's own sources call the DebugSimulateContextLoss()/DebugRestoreContext() channel “one-directional and test-only” (the RendererDeviceEvent comment in IGraphicsRenderer.hpp) and “a deliberate, named test seam” (GraphicsDevice.cpp). A shipped game should therefore not reach it from a player's key press, or only through an explicit debug opt-in.
issues.actual:
• After passing each event to PlatformInputBridge::ProcessEvent, Game::PollEvents calls GraphicsDevice_.GetRenderer().DebugSimulateContextLoss() for a pressed, non-repeated KeyCode::F9 and DebugRestoreContext() for F10, unconditionally (no build, option or opt-out guard). The game still sees the key, and the framework action happens as well. What the press does depends on the renderer (read at 3b43bd86):
  • EasyGL on the desktop: F9 and F10 both print a line to std::cerr, notify MetaGL of a context loss, recreate the native context through the platform, reload the GL entry points and recreate every registered resource. EasyGLTextureRenderer::recreate_gl_resource re-uploads level 0 from the CPU shadow; DXT1/DXT3/DXT5 textures are re-uploaded from their retained compressed blocks (UploadLevel falls back to compressedLevels_ when it is given no pixels); a texture with no surviving shadow (context recovery disabled) is re-created as zeros.
  • DirectX 9: F9 marks the device lost and reports RendererDeviceEvent::Lost; the renderer then refuses CanBeginDrawEXT(), so the game stops drawing until F10 performs the reset.
  • WebGPU: F9 throws System::NotSupportedException while a TextureCube, RenderTargetCube, Texture3D, occlusion query or custom ShaderEffect is alive; nothing in PollEvents, Tick or Run catches it, so natively it ends Run() and in the browser loop it is logged and the loop stops. Without such a resource, F9 releases the device and the game stops drawing until F10.
  • The remaining renderers use the no-op defaults.

issues.title: The Emscripten Game loop (EmscriptenMainLoopCallback) does not implement Game's loop contract
issues.summary: In the browser, Game ignores SuppressDraw and ResetElapsedTime, uses FNA's clock order instead of the XNA rule the desktop loop implements, and turns a frame exception into a normal return from Run() without Exiting.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Game::Run() under Emscripten; IsFixedTimeStep, SuppressDraw(), ResetElapsedTime(), GameTime, the Exiting event
issues.expected: The same Game contract as the native Game::Tick path: variable-step updates when IsFixedTimeStep is false; SuppressDraw() and ResetElapsedTime() honoured; the XNA clock rule CNA measured and pins on the desktop (first update with zero ElapsedGameTime, TotalGameTime as the time before the step); IsRunningSlowly meaningful; and a frame exception leaving Run() as it does natively (Run() logs and rethrows).
issues.actual: Game::EmscriptenMainLoopCallback runs its own clock. With IsFixedTimeStep true it keeps a millisecond accumulator: it caps the delta at 250 ms, drains whole TargetElapsedTime steps, gives the first update a full step and adds each step to TotalGameTime before Update. With IsFixedTimeStep false it runs one Update per frame with the measured time (capped at 250 ms), again adding it to TotalGameTime first. In both modes it forces IsRunningSlowly to false, draws only if an update ran, and never reads suppressDraw_, forceElapsedTimeToZero_ or isSuspended_. Its catch blocks log a frame exception, clear the loop slot and return, so RunLoop ends, Run() calls EndRun() and AfterLoop() and returns normally, and Exiting is never raised.

issues.title: Game::InactiveSleepTime is stored and validated but the loop never sleeps while the game is inactive
issues.summary: InactiveSleepTime is documented in Game.hpp and the C API as how long the loop sleeps while the game is inactive, but nothing in Tick, RunLoop or the browser frame reads it, so an unfocused game keeps its full frame rate.

issues.title: GraphicsDeviceManager leaves dangling references when its lifetime is not nested inside its Game
issues.summary: Game never clears its cached manager and service pointers, the manager never removes its ClientSizeChanged handler, and ~GraphicsDeviceManager dereferences its Game, so a manager that dies before or after its game is a use-after-free.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GraphicsDeviceManager(Game*), ~GraphicsDeviceManager(), GraphicsDeviceManager::Dispose(); Game::getGraphicsDeviceProperty(), Game::BeginDraw()/EndDraw(), Game::Dispose()
issues.expected: Destroying or disposing a GraphicsDeviceManager should leave its game in a consistent state: the services it registered gone and no longer used by the game, its window subscription removed, and its destructor safe regardless of whether the game still exists. The header describes the argument only as “the game that owns this manager” and states no lifetime rule.
issues.actual: Three one-way references survive: (1) registerServices subscribes a lambda capturing this to Window.ClientSizeChanged without keeping a token, and nothing removes it; (2) unregisterServices removes the two service entries, but Game keeps graphicsDeviceService_ and graphicsDeviceManager_, raw pointers cached in getGraphicsDeviceProperty, Initialize and DoInitialize and used by BeginDraw, EndDraw and Dispose(bool); (3) ~GraphicsDeviceManager calls Dispose(false), whose unregisterServices dereferences game_. A manager destroyed while its game keeps running is therefore used after free on the next frame or resize, and a manager that outlives an undisposed game reads the destroyed game in its destructor. CNA's C API states the same finding (“a canonical defect rather than anything this ABI can validate away”) and works around it by keeping every released manager alive until its game is destroyed.

issues.title: PhoneApplicationService::getCurrentProperty()'s static instance detaches from an already-destroyed Game during static destruction
issues.summary: The process-wide PhoneApplicationService is a function-local static holding a borrowed Game*; attached to a Game that is destroyed first, its destructor calls DetachEXT on the dead game's events.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Phone::Shell::PhoneApplicationService::getCurrentProperty(), AttachEXT(Game&), DetachEXT() and ~PhoneApplicationService()
issues.expected: The header presents getCurrentProperty() as “the application's single lifecycle service” and AttachEXT as the one line a phone port writes. DetachEXT's documentation says the destructor calls it “so a game that outlives nothing in particular still leaves no dangling subscription behind”. Using the process-wide instance with an ordinary Game should end the process without undefined behaviour.
issues.actual: getCurrentProperty() returns a function-local static PhoneApplicationService, destroyed during static destruction after main returns. AttachEXT stores a raw Game* and three event tokens; nothing in Game or elsewhere under modules/runtime knows about the service, so nothing clears the pointer when the game is destroyed. ~PhoneApplicationService calls DetachEXT, which calls Activated.Remove, Deactivated.Remove and Exiting.Remove through the stored pointer. When the Game lived on main's stack, the usual shape of a port, those calls erase from the handler vectors of a destroyed object: a use-after-free at exit.
