issues.title: StorageDevice::EnsureStorageRoot caches the process-wide storage root in unsynchronised statics
issues.summary: The storage root is cached in a plain static bool and std::string with no lock or atomic, so two threads touching storage for the first time both resolve it and write the string concurrently, a data race, and a reader may see the flag before the string.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Storage::StorageDevice::GetStorageRootEXT() (“Absolute path to the storage root”) and every storage operation that resolves the root
issues.expected: GetStorageRootEXT() and the container operations built on it always see the absolute root. SetAppNameEXT is documented to be called once at startup before storage is used, so renaming concurrently is a caller error, but two threads touching storage for the first time is not prohibited anywhere.
issues.actual: EnsureStorageRoot in {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp|StorageDevice.cpp}} tests storageRootInitialized_, resolves the path, assigns storageRoot_ and sets the flag last. That order was corrected by 8a67da536, which removed the single-threaded empty-root latch. storageRoot_, appName_ and storageRootInitialized_ are still plain statics with no lock or atomic. Two threads that arrive before the first resolution finishes both resolve the root and both assign the std::string, a data race (undefined behaviour). Nothing orders the plain bool store after the string store, so another core may see the flag set while the string is still being written.

sources.note: StorageDevice::EnsureStorageRoot (flag set after storageRoot_, no lock), SetAppNameEXT, GetStorageRootEXT
static storageRoot_, appName_, storageRootInitialized_; GetStorageRootEXT and SetAppNameEXT documentation

issues.evidence:
Checked by reading {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp|StorageDevice.cpp}} and its header at 3b43bd86. The race is a consequence of the statement order; it was not provoked. Not executed.

Re-verified at b0e97bb1: 8a67da536 (SAMPLE-070) moved the flag after the assignment; the three statics in StorageDevice.hpp are still unsynchronised. Not executed.
issues.tests_current: {{src:modules/storage/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Storage/StorageDeviceTests.cpp|StorageDeviceTests.cpp}} is single-threaded; no test covers concurrent first access.
issues.regression_test: A ThreadSanitizer test that resets the root with SetAppNameEXT and then calls GetStorageRootEXT() from several threads at once, expecting the same non-empty absolute path from every thread and no reported race.
issues.blast_radius: Games that save or query storage from more than one thread before the root has been resolved once (for example a background save racing the first storage query of the main thread). Single-threaded storage use, and any use after the first successful resolution, is unaffected.

issues.title: StorageDevice::getFreeSpaceProperty, getTotalSpaceProperty and getIsConnectedProperty pass the UTF-8 root to std::filesystem through the narrow path constructor
issues.summary: The three device properties hand the UTF-8 root string straight to fs::exists, fs::space and fs::path, which on Windows reinterpret it in the ANSI code page, so with a non-ASCII root they query a different path.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Storage::StorageDevice::getFreeSpaceProperty(), getTotalSpaceProperty() and getIsConnectedProperty()
issues.expected: CNA's path model ({{src:docs/filesystem-path-model.md}}, rule 2): a std::string holding a path is UTF-8 and "is converted back into a std::filesystem::path before it touches the filesystem again", through PathFromUtf8 ({{src:modules/core/include/CNA/Internal/PathUtf8.hpp|PathUtf8.hpp}}). Every other storage operation follows that rule.
issues.actual: In {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp|StorageDevice.cpp}}, getFreeSpaceProperty and getTotalSpaceProperty call fs::exists(root) and fs::space(root) with the std::string root, and getIsConnectedProperty builds fs::path p(root). On POSIX the bytes pass through unchanged. On Windows the narrow constructor reads the string through the process ANSI code page, so every non-ASCII character in the root, including one the code page can spell (the two UTF-8 bytes of e-acute become two other characters), yields a different path. That affects a root containing such a character in the user profile path, in LOCALAPPDATA or in the application name given to SetAppNameEXT: fs::exists reports false, the space properties return LLONG_MAX ("unlimited") instead of the real figure, and getIsConnectedProperty walks up from the wrong path.

sources.note: getFreeSpaceProperty, getTotalSpaceProperty and getIsConnectedProperty use the std::string root directly
PathFromUtf8, the conversion every other storage path uses
rule 2: a narrow path string is UTF-8 and is converted before it touches the filesystem

issues.evidence:
Checked by reading {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp|StorageDevice.cpp}} and the path model at 3b43bd86; not exercised on Windows. Every other path in {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp|StorageDevice.cpp}} and {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp|StorageContainer.cpp}} converts with PathFromUtf8, and EnsureStorageRoot reads the environment with GetEnvironmentVariableW precisely so that non-ASCII roots survive; these three properties are the remaining narrow sites in the module.

Independent re-verification: Checked by reading {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp|StorageDevice.cpp}} and the path model at 3b43bd86; not exercised on Windows. Every other path in {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp|StorageDevice.cpp}} and {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp|StorageContainer.cpp}} converts with PathFromUtf8, and EnsureStorageRoot reads the environment with GetEnvironmentVariableW precisely so that non-ASCII roots survive; these three properties are the remaining narrow sites in the module. The Windows consequence rests on the standard library's narrow-to-wide conversion through the ANSI code page: CNA's own spikes/windows-unicode-path-spike records the ANSI behaviour of path::string() and of fopen given UTF-8 bytes (which fails for representable names such as cafe with an accent too) but did not measure the path(std::string) constructor itself, and a search of the tree finds no manifest that sets a UTF-8 active code page. The basis is therefore inferred, not executed. Tests: CApi_StorageSmoke (C ABI builds only) calls the free-space, total-space and connection queries on an ASCII root; nothing runs them on a non-ASCII root.
issues.reproduction:
// Illustrative, Windows with ANSI code page 1252; not run.
StorageDevice::SetAppNameEXT("Hra\xC4\x8D");   // "Hrac" with c-caron (U+010D) in UTF-8; not in code page 1252
auto device = StorageDevice::EndShowSelector(
    StorageDevice::BeginShowSelector(nullptr, nullptr).get());
long long freeBytes = device->getFreeSpaceProperty();   // LLONG_MAX: the narrowed root does not exist
issues.tests_current: {{src:modules/storage/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Storage/StorageDeviceTests.cpp|StorageDeviceTests.cpp}} tests none of the three properties; UnicodePathResolutionTests.cpp covers the core helpers, not storage.
issues.regression_test: A Windows test with a non-ASCII application name expecting getFreeSpaceProperty() to equal fs::space(PathFromUtf8(GetStorageRootEXT())).available and getIsConnectedProperty() to be true; the fix is PathFromUtf8 in all three properties.
issues.blast_radius: Windows users whose data root or application name contains characters outside the ANSI code page: free-space checks see unlimited space and the connection check examines the wrong directory. POSIX hosts, ASCII roots and every container file operation are unaffected.
issues.workaround: Keep the application name ASCII, and do not rely on the space properties when the Windows profile path is non-ASCII.

issues.title: HttpNotificationChannel answers length-less and chunked pushes with 200 and reads request bodies of unbounded size
issues.summary: ReadRequestBody's comment says unreadable pushes are refused, but a request without Content-Length (chunked included) still gets 200 and is dropped, and the declared length is never bounded. A short body is now refused with 400.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Phone::Notification::HttpNotificationChannel listener: the HTTP status a push sender receives and the bytes raised as HttpNotificationReceived
issues.expected: The comment above ReadRequestBody states the design: the channel “understands a request with a Content-Length and nothing else”, and chunked encoding and other forms “are not accepted rather than half-supported -- a push that this cannot read is better refused visibly than delivered truncated”. A sender should get an error status for a request the channel cannot read, and a raised notification should carry the whole body.
issues.actual: ReadRequestBody reads until the blank line that ends the header block (a failed or closed connection, or a header block over 1 MiB, returns false and the worker answers 400). It then looks for content-length: anywhere in the lower-cased header block and parses it with strtoul; without it the length is 0. A request without Content-Length, including a chunked one, is therefore answered 200 OK and dropped (an empty body is never queued). The declared length is never capped, so the worker's buffer grows with whatever a peer declares and sends.

sources.note: ReadRequestBody (header loop, Content-Length search, body loop that now refuses a short body) and Listen (200/400 reply, queueing)
only complete requests with a Content-Length are sent
truncated and partial-request cases (400 path); no chunked or length-less case

Checked by reading {{src:modules/phone/src/HttpNotificationChannel.cpp|HttpNotificationChannel.cpp}} at 3b43bd86. Not executed. The phone module's Development page already records the same response table as a maintainer note.

The length-less and unbounded-length halves are unchanged.

No test sends a chunked, length-less or oversized request.

issues.title: Two open HttpNotificationChannel objects with the same name leave Find unable to locate one that is still open
issues.summary: Open assigns the registry entry for the name without checking for an existing channel, and when the later channel closes first it erases the name while the earlier one is still listening, so Find returns null for a live channel.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Phone::Notification::HttpNotificationChannel constructor, Open(), Close() and static Find(const std::string&)
issues.expected: Find is documented to return “The channel, or null when no channel of that name is open”. The constructor documents the name as “unique within the application”, and Close erases the registry entry only when it still points at the closing channel, which shows the registry is meant to survive a replaced entry. Either a duplicate Open should be refused, or Find should keep answering while any channel of that name is open.
issues.actual: Open does Registry()[channelName_] = this under the registry mutex, silently replacing an earlier channel. With channels A and B of one name both open, Find returns B. If B closes first, its Close finds the entry pointing at itself and erases the name although A is still listening, so Find returns null for a live channel. Nothing refuses or logs the duplicate.

issues.title: A handler that throws during HttpNotificationChannel::DispatchPendingNotificationsEXT discards every remaining notification of that batch
issues.summary: DispatchPendingNotificationsEXT moves the whole queue into a local vector before raising; an exception from a HttpNotificationReceived handler propagates and destroys the notifications not yet raised.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Phone::Notification::HttpNotificationChannel::DispatchPendingNotificationsEXT() and HttpNotificationReceived
issues.expected: The method is documented as “Raises the events of every notification that has arrived.” A notification that arrived but had not been raised when an earlier handler threw should not disappear: a later call should still raise it, or the method should document that a throwing handler loses the batch.
issues.actual: The method swaps pending_ into a local vector under mutex_, releases the lock and raises HttpNotificationReceived once per body. Sharp Runtime's EventHandler::Raise invokes handlers without catching, so the first exception leaves the loop and the local vector, holding every body after the throwing one, is destroyed. The next dispatch sees only notifications that arrived after the swap.

issues.title: The phone notification channel and sender never initialise Winsock or link ws2_32, so on Windows they work only if something else did
issues.summary: modules/phone calls no WSAStartup and its library names no Winsock import library, so on Windows Open and SendAsync work only after another component initialised Winsock. Its INVALID_SOCKET checks were fixed on 2026-10-22.
issues.public_contract: HttpNotificationChannel::Open() and RawPushNotificationMessage / ToastPushNotificationMessage::SendAsync on Windows
issues.expected: CNA builds the notification path for Windows on purpose: cmake/UnitTests.cmake (WINNATIVE-0014) says “The channel ITSELF is built on Windows ... this excludes the test's POSIX listener, not the feature”, and CNA's native-Windows plan records two compile fixes in these files. Winsock requires WSAStartup before socket or getaddrinfo; CNA's own Inspector socket layer calls it for exactly that reason.
issues.actual: No file under modules/phone calls WSAStartup; among CNA's own sources only the Inspector's {{src:modules/inspector/src/InternalSocket.cpp|InternalSocket.cpp}} does (besides the vendored ENet's initialisation). In a process where neither ran, socket() fails with WSANOTINITIALISED: Open queues a ChannelOpenFailed error, logs that it could not create a listening socket and returns with no URI, and SendAsync fails at getaddrinfo and returns false. {{src:modules/phone/CMakeLists.txt|modules/phone/CMakeLists.txt}} links cna_phone to no ws2_32; the only phone target that names it is the MinGW build of the lifecycle test, which also calls WSAStartup itself.

issues.workaround: Call WSAStartup(MAKEWORD(2, 2), &data) in the host before opening a channel or sending, and link ws2_32 explicitly.

issues.title: HttpNotificationChannel's listener spins without backoff on a persistent accept error
issues.summary: When accept fails while the channel is still listening (EMFILE or ENFILE when descriptors run out, ENOBUFS), the listener thread retries at once with no delay, so a persistent failure makes it loop at full speed.
issues.public_contract: HttpNotificationChannel::Close() and the channel's internal listener thread
issues.expected: A failure the listener thread cannot recover from by retrying immediately should not consume a core: the worker should back off, or report the failure and stop.
issues.actual: When accept returns an invalid socket while listening_ is still true, Listen continues its loop at once. EMFILE leaves the pending connection queued, so the next accept fails the same way and the loop spins at full speed until the condition clears. Not part of this entry: Open's plain if (listening_) check, which is not a compare-exchange; the header promises no thread safety for Open, and the Development page tells callers to keep Open and Close on one owning thread.

sources.note: Listen (continue on a failed accept while listening_), Close (keeps the descriptor until the worker joined)
Close against idle, partial and complete connections; no descriptor exhaustion

Checked by reading {{src:modules/phone/src/HttpNotificationChannel.cpp|HttpNotificationChannel.cpp}} at 3b43bd86. Not executed.

Narrowed at c6dec91f: 20fe6efd2 (MUSEUM-PHONE-001, 2026-10-22) removed the data race this entry also described: the worker now receives the listening socket by value when it starts, and Close keeps that descriptor open until the worker has joined, so it can no longer be reused for an unrelated socket while the worker still uses it. The accept-error loop is unchanged.

issues.blast_radius: Processes with an open channel under descriptor or kernel buffer exhaustion; a normal channel is unaffected.

issues.title: LocalGamerServicesStore maps distinct gamertags to one achievements file when they differ only in characters outside A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-'
issues.summary: SanitizeStoreFileNameComponent replaces every other byte with an underscore, so gamertags such as "Ann B" and "Ann_B", or two same-length non-ASCII names, share one achievements file and see each other's achievements.
issues.public_contract: SignedInGamer::AwardAchievement and GetAchievements persistence (CNA::Internal::GamerServices::SaveEarnedAchievementEXT, LoadEarnedAchievementsEXT, SanitizeStoreFileNameComponent)
issues.expected: Achievements belong to one gamer: GetAchievements returns what that gamertag earned and nothing another gamer earned.
issues.actual: The achievements file is achievements/<SanitizeStoreFileNameComponent(gamertag)>.json ({{src:modules/gamer-services/src/Internal/LocalGamerServicesStore.cpp|LocalGamerServicesStore.cpp}}). The sanitiser keeps ASCII letters, digits, -, _ and ., replaces every other byte with _ (each byte of a multi-byte UTF-8 character separately) and maps an empty name to _. The mapping is many-to-one and the file does not record the original gamertag, so "Ann B", "Ann_B" and "Ann!B" read and write one list, as do two non-ASCII names whose characters have the same byte lengths. Leaderboards are not affected in the same way: each board file stores every entry's raw gamertag.

issues.title: NetworkSession::GamerJoined reports a gamer added with AddLocalGamer twice to a handler subscribed between that call and the next Update
issues.summary: AddLocalGamer inserts the new gamer into AllGamers at once and queues its GamerJoin event for the next Update, while subscribing replays GamerJoined for every gamer already in AllGamers, so a handler subscribed in that window is called twice for the new gamer.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::NetworkSession::GamerJoined (subscription replay) with NetworkSession::AddLocalGamer and the transport's AddRemoteGamer
issues.expected: Each subscriber sees one GamerJoined per gamer: subscribing replays the gamers already present, later joins are raised once. XNA's AddLocalGamer is asynchronous, so the gamer enters the collections and its event is raised inside one Update call and user code cannot subscribe between the two. CNA's constructor comment states the same intent, avoiding a queued event that would double-fire a replayed join.
issues.actual: AddLocalGamer adds the gamer to LocalGamers and AllGamers immediately and pushes a GamerJoin event that Update raises later. The replay hook installed by the constructor calls each new handler once for every gamer in allGamers_ at subscription time, so a handler subscribed after AddLocalGamer and before the next Update receives the new gamer's join twice. The AddRemoteGamer path (used by the transport inside Update) inserts and queues the same way, but a handler can subscribe in that window only from inside another GamerJoined handler, which XNA's own add accessor and ProcessGamerJoined reproduce, so it is not part of this entry.

sources.note: constructor SetReplayHook and its comment; AddLocalGamer; AddRemoteGamer; Update's GamerJoin branch

issues.title: A joined SystemLink session answers LAN discovery for itself, so Find lists the session once per member
issues.summary: Every SystemLink session, including a joined one, registers with discovery and ReplyToQuery ignores IsHost, so Find lists a session once per member; joining through a client's entry is refused by that client instead of reaching the host.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::NetworkSession::Find and Join for NetworkSessionType::SystemLink (ENetDiscoveryService::RegisterHost and ReplyToQuery; ENetBackend::StartHosting and HandleClientHello)
issues.expected: XNA's Find returns the available sessions, one entry per hosted session, and joining an entry connects to that session's host. CNA's discovery code itself describes the reply as coming from a hosting session.
issues.actual: The NetworkSession constructor calls ENetBackend::StartHosting for every SystemLink session, including the one EndJoin constructs with isHost false, and StartHosting calls ENetDiscoveryService::RegisterHost(session, port) ({{src:modules/net/src/Internal/ENetBackend.cpp|ENetBackend.cpp}}). ReplyToQuery in {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/ENetDiscoveryService.cpp|ENetDiscoveryService.cpp}} answers any query with a matching type filter with the registered session's port, gamer counts and host gamertag, without checking that the session is the host. A client therefore advertises the session it joined: with host A and client B, a Find on machine C returns two entries with the same host gamertag (results are de-duplicated by connect port, and the ports differ). If C joins B's entry, B's HandleClientHello now sees that its HostPeer names another machine, logs a warning and disconnects C, so the join fails although the session C saw is open. That every peer keeps an accepting ENet host is intended (host migration reuses it); the discovery registration is what exposes it.

issues.title: Setting Game::IsMouseVisible throws PlatformException on the terminal platform when the terminal reports mouse input
issues.summary: Game::setIsMouseVisibleProperty forwards to IPlatformMouse::SetCursorVisible whenever a window and a mouse service exist; the terminal platform supplies a TerminalMouse whenever stdin and stdout are both terminals (TerminalCapabilities::canQuery is isatty(stdin), independent of whether the emulator answers any query), and that mouse always throws.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Game::setIsMouseVisibleProperty(bool); CNA::Platform::IPlatformMouse::SetCursorVisible(bool) on the terminal platform
issues.expected: XNA's IsMouseVisible setter never throws, and ported XNA games commonly set it in their constructor. CNA's own test for the property (SettingMouseVisibilityIsSafeWithNoPointerService) states that the setter must work whether or not the platform has a mouse, and expects the terminal to take the same no-pointer path as the headless platform.
issues.actual: Game::setIsMouseVisibleProperty records the value and then, when GraphicsDevice_ has a platform window and platform_->GetMouse() is non-null, calls SetCursorVisible(value). On the terminal platform the window exists only for the SOFTWARE renderer (the one family that asks for a surface presenter) on a TTY; GraphicsDevice creates it during Game construction. TerminalPlatform::GetMouse() runs EnsureCapabilitiesDetected, which creates a TerminalMouse whenever DetectTerminalCapabilities reports canQuery; canQuery is isatty(stdin) on top of isatty(stdout) and is set before any query is sent, so every interactive terminal session gets the mouse, whether or not the emulator answers the capability queries or supports mouse reporting. TerminalMouse::SetCursorVisible unconditionally throws PlatformException (a terminal cannot control its emulator's graphical pointer). The setter does not catch it, so IsMouseVisible = true in a game's constructor ends construction in an interactive terminal. With stdin or stdout redirected there is no mouse service (and, for stdout, no window), and the call is a no-op. CNA's own {{src:plans/plan_platform.md|plan_platform.md}} PLAT-49 records that IsMouseVisible was meant to be a determinate no-op under HEADLESS and, later, TERMINAL; PLAT-139 later gave the terminal mouse a service that refuses visibility changes.

issues.title: The Headless and Terminal window constructors accept BorderlessFullscreen although their own SetFullscreenMode refuses it
issues.summary: Both capability-minimal windows store WindowDescription::fullscreenMode directly at construction instead of routing it through SetFullscreenMode, so a window created in BorderlessFullscreen reports that mode though the platform's capability is false.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Platform::IPlatform::CreateWindow(const WindowDescription&) and IPlatformWindow::GetFullscreenMode()/SetFullscreenMode() on the Headless and Terminal platforms
issues.expected: {{src:docs/platform-abstraction.md|platform-abstraction.md}} and IPlatformWindow::SetFullscreenMode state that “a window with no borderlessFullscreen capability must refuse that mode”, and the SDL3 platform enforces it: its CreateWindow ({{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3Platform.cpp|Sdl3Platform.cpp}}) funnels a non-Windowed WindowDescription::fullscreenMode through SetFullscreenMode right after construction, so the refusal path runs. Headless and Terminal report borderlessFullscreen = false and their SetFullscreenMode throws PlatformNotSupportedException(BorderlessFullscreen).
issues.actual: {{src:modules/platform/src/Headless/HeadlessPlatform.cpp|HeadlessWindow}} and {{src:modules/platform/src/Terminal/TerminalPlatform.cpp|TerminalWindow}} initialise mode_(description.fullscreenMode) in their constructors and never call their own SetFullscreenMode. A window created with fullscreenMode = BorderlessFullscreen is therefore accepted, and GetFullscreenMode() returns BorderlessFullscreen, even though the platform's capability is false and a later SetFullscreenMode(BorderlessFullscreen) on the same window throws. The window is left in a mode the platform says it cannot provide.

The XNA-facing runtime cannot reach it: GraphicsDevice creates its window with the default Windowed mode and later calls SetFullscreenMode with ExclusiveFullscreen or Windowed only, so the path is reached only by code that calls IPlatform::CreateWindow directly with BorderlessFullscreen.

issues.title: Sdl3Platform reports the nativeFileDialog capability on iOS and web builds, where SDL has no usable file-dialog backend
issues.summary: The SDL3 platform sets nativeFileDialog unconditionally, so on iOS and the web the platform says a dialog can be shown while FileDialog::getIsSupportedProperty says it cannot, and FileDialog::Show* reach SDL, which fails the request.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Platform::PlatformCapabilities::nativeFileDialog as reported by the SDL3 platform (Sdl3Platform::GetCapabilities); CNA::Devices::FileDialog::getIsSupportedProperty and ShowOpenFile, ShowSaveFile, ShowOpenFolder
issues.expected: {{src:modules/platform/include/CNA/Platform/PlatformCapabilities.hpp|PlatformCapabilities.hpp}}: nativeFileDialog means "A native file or folder dialog can be shown", and a capability that is not supported is refused, never silently ignored. {{src:modules/devices-ext/include/CNA/Devices/FileDialog.hpp|FileDialog.hpp}} records that SDL has no dialog backend for iOS or Web/Emscripten and promises that getIsSupportedProperty() "reports this honestly per platform"; a Show* call there should take the documented unavailable path.
issues.actual: Sdl3Platform::GetCapabilities in {{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3Platform.cpp|Sdl3Platform.cpp}} sets capabilities.nativeFileDialog = true with no target condition, although primarySelection in the same function is guarded for Emscripten and Android. FileDialog::getIsSupportedProperty compensates with its own build-target switch (Web and iOS return false), but the three Show* functions, and any other reader of the capability, gate on the capability alone, so on those targets the request reaches Sdl3Dialogs and SDL. On iOS SDL builds its dummy dialog, which reports failure through the callback at once; in a browser SDL's Unix dialog code finds neither a desktop portal nor a helper process and does the same. ResultTrampoline in {{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3SystemServices.cpp|Sdl3SystemServices.cpp}} turns SDL's null file list into an empty list, so the caller sees the same answer as a cancel, before Show* returns. That is also what FileDialog's own unavailable path delivers (ReportUnavailable calls back with an empty list immediately), so the result and timing a Show* caller observes are the same on both paths; what contradicts itself is the two public answers, the capability (true) and getIsSupportedProperty (false). The null parent window the candidate also lists is a documented note in {{src:modules/devices-ext/include/CNA/Devices/FileDialog.hpp|FileDialog.hpp}} and is not part of this defect.

issues.title: The SDL3 file-dialog and tray-entry trampolines call application callbacks without a try/catch, so a throwing handler unwinds through SDL's C code
issues.summary: ResultTrampoline and EntryClickTrampoline invoke the application's std::function directly from SDL C callbacks, so an exception escaping it crosses SDL frames (undefined behaviour, typically std::terminate).
issues.public_contract: CNA::Devices::FileDialog result callbacks and CNA::Devices::SystemTray entry-click callbacks on the SDL3 platform
issues.expected: CNA's own devices event contract ({{src:docs/devices-event-contract.md|devices-event-contract.md}}, section 6, Exception semantics) states the decided policy: an unhandled exception escaping a user-supplied handler must never propagate across a C callback boundary, and the normative rule is log-and-continue, catching at the C-callback or thread-entry boundary and making the event observable. The Accelerometer and Gyroscope dispatch path follows it. FileDialog.hpp and SystemTray.hpp neither state that handlers must not throw nor catch on the caller's behalf.
issues.actual: ResultTrampoline in {{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3SystemServices.cpp|Sdl3SystemServices.cpp}} builds the path list and calls context->callback(paths); EntryClickTrampoline in {{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3Tray.cpp|Sdl3Tray.cpp}} calls (*callback)(). Both are passed to SDL as C function pointers and have no try/catch. FileDialog.hpp notes the result may arrive “on a different thread than the one the call” was made on.

EntryClickTrampoline
callback threading note; no exception rule

Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; the file-dialog half was also executed (see below), the tray half was only read.

The contract is CNA's own devices event contract, section 6 of which is titled 'decided but not yet uniformly implemented' and lists sensor paths only, so the SDL3 dialog and tray boundaries are an unlisted instance of that policy. Neither devices-ext wrapper adds a catch (FileDialog.cpp passes the callback straight to the platform and SystemTray.cpp forwards it), so a handler's exception reaches the trampoline. What SDL's C frames then do with it (undefined behaviour, typically std::terminate) depends on the toolchain and was not run.

Independent re-verification: Checked by reading at 3b43bd86. Reproduced for the file dialog by the audit at 009d40f5: Sdl3SystemServices.cpp was compiled with g++ -O0 and linked with a system SDL 3.4.0 (not CNA's pinned SDL commit); Sdl3Dialogs::ShowOpenFileDialog was called with a callback that throws, SDL's zenity driver delivered the (cancelled) result on its own thread through ResultTrampoline, and the process ended with 'terminate called after throwing an instance of std::runtime_error' (SIGABRT). The SystemTray entry-click trampoline was read but not run. Neither devices-ext wrapper adds a catch (FileDialog.cpp passes the callback straight to the platform and SystemTray.cpp forwards it). What SDL's C frames do with an exception delivered on the calling thread depends on the toolchain: with default x86-64 unwind tables it unwinds through them, without unwind tables it terminates.

issues.workaround: Catch every exception inside the handler.

issues.expected: modules/CMakeLists.txt documents AUTO as “use FFmpeg only when all required pkg-config modules are present” and ON as reporting an unsupported configuration immediately. issues.title: cmake/toolchains/mingw-w64.cmake falls back to the i686 compiler but keeps CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR x86_64, so 32-bit and 64-bit trees share one persistent SDL install directory
issues.summary: When x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc is missing the toolchain silently selects i686-w64-mingw32 yet still declares x86_64, which names the .sdl-prebuilt-Windows-x86_64 install; since the SDL build manifest records the compiler, the two trees no longer reuse each other's SDL but rebuild that one install in turn. Its header comment also still requires a pre-built SDL on CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH.
issues.public_contract: cmake/toolchains/mingw-w64.cmake (MinGW-w64 cross toolchain file)
issues.expected: A toolchain file should either target the architecture it declares or fail. {{src:cmake/ThirdPartySDL.cmake|ThirdPartySDL.cmake}} keys its persistent SDL install by ${CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME}-${CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR} precisely so that differently targeted builds cannot reuse one another's SDL.
issues.actual: The toolchain sets CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR x86_64 unconditionally, then picks i686-w64-mingw32 when x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc is not found. A host with only the 32-bit MinGW compilers therefore builds a 32-bit tree whose SDL install is keyed Windows-x86_64 - the same key, and so the same install directory, as a real 64-bit cross build. Since 9bb8beb29, 01a59fdd9 and 2e98818e5 (2026-10-26 dependency audit C-09) the SDL build manifest ({{src:cmake/SdlPrebuiltFingerprint.cmake|SdlPrebuiltFingerprint.cmake}}) also records the toolchain file's content, the compiler it resolved to and the settings it decided, read by {{src:cmake/SdlToolchainSettings.cmake|SdlToolchainSettings.cmake}} in a cmake -P evaluation, so a tree whose compiler differs no longer reuses the other's SDL: it finds the manifest changed and rebuilds the shared install in place. A 32-bit and a 64-bit tree therefore rebuild it in turn, and CNA records that such a shared install can change under the other tree's running build ({{src:handoff.md|handoff.md}} section 5.2). The header comment still tells the user to put pre-built SDL3/SDL3_image/SDL3_mixer on CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH, although the vendored SDL is built for the target at configure time into that keyed install.

issues.title: Delta-maintained diagnostics gauges such as Audio/AllocatedVoices drift after a runtime OFF window
issues.summary: GaugeHandle::Add discards deltas while the runtime mode is OFF, so a gauge kept with GAUGE_ADD(+1/-1), such as Audio/AllocatedVoices, stays wrong (too high, or negative) after statistics are re-enabled, until mixer shutdown resets it.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Diagnostics::GaugeHandle::Add and CNA_DIAGNOSTICS_GAUGE_ADD across SetRuntimeMode(Mode::Off); the documented meaning of Audio/AllocatedVoices
issues.expected: docs/diagnostics.md: gauges retain the latest value, and Audio/AllocatedVoices is a “gauge, exact at the mixer facade” counting “mixer tracks CNA has allocated and not logically destroyed”. After statistics are re-enabled an exact gauge reports the true count, or the limitation is documented as it is for resources created while OFF.
issues.actual: AddMetric and SetMetric return without writing while the runtime mode is OFF. Both mixer back-ends maintain the gauge with deltas, +1 in CreateMixerTrack and −1 in DestroyMixerTrack, and only EndMixerEngineShutdown sets it to 0. A track created before an OFF window and destroyed during it leaves the gauge one too high; one created during it and destroyed afterwards leaves it at −1. Nothing resynchronises the value, and the known-limitations list names only the resource-registry effect.

issues.title: On Emscripten a diagnostics frame excludes the requestAnimationFrame wait, so FrameSample.framesPerSecond is a work rate there
issues.summary: The web loop opens the frame scope inside EmscriptenMainLoopCallback and waits for the next animation frame after it returns, so web frame durations and FPS exclude pacing, unlike the native Tick the documentation describes.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Diagnostics::FrameSample (durationNs, framesPerSecond) as published by Game's frame scope
issues.expected: docs/diagnostics.md: “Native Game::Tick and the Emscripten main-loop callback publish one frame ... The top-level tick measurement includes fixed-step pacing waits”. A frame should mean the same on both loops, or the difference should be documented.
issues.actual: Native: CNA_DIAGNOSTICS_FRAME_SCOPE() opens at the top of Game::Tick, which contains the fixed-step Delay/yield loop, so a frame spans the pacing wait and framesPerSecond tracks the target rate. Emscripten: Game::RunLoop calls EmscriptenMainLoopCallback(), whose body holds the frame scope and the Game/Tick zone and paces with an accumulator that never waits, and then calls CNA_WaitForAnimationFrame() (an EM_ASYNC_JS await on requestAnimationFrame) outside it. A web frame's durationNs therefore covers event polling, updates and drawing only, and framesPerSecond (1e9 / durationNs) reports how fast that work ran, for example 500 for 2 ms of work at a 60 Hz display.

issues.title: Inspector ServerHello.graphicsRenderer reports the compile-time default renderer, not the one GraphicsRendererSelection actually created
issues.summary: The Inspector session names the build's default renderer identity, so in a multi-renderer build where a preference, the environment variable or a fallback selects another renderer, the Session view shows the wrong one.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Inspector::HelloResponse::graphicsRenderer (the Session view's renderer) versus CNA::GraphicsRendererSelection::GetActive()
issues.expected: The Session view's renderer is the one the application runs on: GraphicsRendererSelection::GetActive() once a device exists (GetSelected() before, since GetActive() throws until the selection is latched).
issues.actual: Agent::Impl::HandleClient sets hello.graphicsRenderer = CNA::getCurrentGraphicsRendererName(), a compile-time constant derived from the CNA_RENDERER_* macro that cmake/RendererSelection.cmake defines project-wide for the default identity only. issues.title: A diagnostics name or resource label longer than 4,096 bytes makes every Inspector snapshot or event batch that contains it fail with LimitExceeded
issues.summary: Diagnostics accepts names up to 1 MiB and labels of any length, but the Inspector protocol caps strings at 4,096 bytes and refuses the whole response, so one long name breaks the affected Inspector views for the rest of the process.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Inspector protocol v1 SnapshotResponse and EventsResponse encoding (ProtocolCodec::Encode) over diagnostics provider v1 data
issues.expected: The Inspector is a consumer of the unchanged provider v1 contract, and {{src:docs/inspector.md|inspector.md}} says oversized complete snapshots are refused rather than partially mislabeled. That refusal policy is therefore intended, but it should be predictable: either the two modules agree on one string bound that registration enforces and the documentation states, or the refusal is limited to the offending item instead of every snapshot and event batch that contains it.
issues.actual: RegisterMetric and RegisterName accept names up to MaximumTraceNameBytes (1 MiB); CopyResource copies labels and formats without a bound. Protocol.cpp's Writer::String throws std::length_error above MaximumStringBytes (4,096) for metric names (WriteMetric, including per-frame metrics), resource label and format (WriteResource) and resolved event names, and Agent::Impl::HandleRequest turns that into ErrorCode::LimitExceeded for the whole request. Metrics are never unregistered, so the overview request (metrics and frames) fails for the rest of the process; the Resources view fails while such a resource lives, and each event batch containing such a name fails. docs/inspector.md says oversized complete snapshots are refused rather than partially mislabeled, but neither states the 4,096-byte bound nor offers a remedy for a long name (its troubleshooting line says only “reduce event count or preview bounds”). Engine labels are short literals ("Texture2D"), so the trigger is application instrumentation.

issues.title: Agent::Stop can wait up to about six seconds for a connection that the accept loop takes around the time Stop runs
issues.summary: Stop shuts down only a client already published as activeClient_, and the worker never re-checks stopping_ after accepting. A connection accepted just before Stop, or during the accept poll of up to 200 ms that follows Stop setting stopping_, is therefore never shut down, and join waits on that client's handshake reads, up to 3 s for the header and 3 s for the payload.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Inspector::Agent::Stop() and ~Agent()
issues.expected: Stop is built to return promptly: it sets stopping_, shuts the active client socket down under socketMutex_ so that a blocked receive returns, and joins a worker whose accept loop wakes every 200 ms.
issues.actual: Agent::Impl::Run publishes an accepted socket as activeClient_ (under socketMutex_) only after AcceptTcp returns, and HandleClient starts the handshake without re-checking stopping_. Stop sets stopping_, shuts down whatever activeClient_ holds at that moment (InvalidSocket when nothing is published) and joins. The worker only notices stopping_ when its 200 ms accept poll times out, and the poll returns at once when a connection arrives, so a connection accepted just before Stop or at any point in that interval is published after Stop's shutdown step and served anyway. HandleClient then blocks in ReceivePacket, which applies HandshakeTimeoutMilliseconds (3,000) to the 24-byte header and again to the payload. A client that sends a valid ClientHello at once ends the wait early; a silent local peer holds Stop, and therefore a game's ~Agent, for about 3 s, and one that sends a complete header and withholds the payload for up to about 6 s.

issues.title: cna_graphics_resource_get_graphics_device returns CNA_RESULT_INVALID_HANDLE for every resource created on a caller-created GraphicsDevice
issues.summary: A resource made on a device from cna_graphics_device_create carries that device's handle as its owner token, and the route passes it to the game-only BorrowGameGraphicsDevice, so asking such a valid resource for its device always fails.
issues.public_contract: cna_graphics_resource_get_graphics_device(CNA_Handle resource, CNA_Handle* out_graphics_device) (CNA/C/graphics_resource.h) for resources created on a cna_graphics_device_create device
issues.expected: graphics_device.h says a caller-created device's handle “is accepted everywhere a borrowed device handle is” and that “resources remember which device made them”; graphics_resource.h promises success with CNA_INVALID_HANDLE for a standalone resource and the owning device's handle for a device-owned one. A valid resource on a live caller-created device should therefore yield that device's handle, or a documented refusal such as CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED, never a claim that a handle is invalid.
issues.actual: cna_graphics_device_create builds the device's view as BorrowedGraphicsDevice{device, own handle}, so every resource created on it stores the device handle in its parentGame owner token (for example IndexBufferResource, CreateOwnedTexture2D). cna_graphics_resource_get_graphics_device sees a non-null device pointer and a non-invalid owner and calls BorrowGameGraphicsDevice(parentGame, ...), which calls GetGame; HandleRegistry::Get finds a slot of kind OwnedGraphicsDevice where it expects Game and answers CNA_RESULT_INVALID_HANDLE, reported as “The CNA game handle is invalid for this call.” The route thus fails for every such resource, while the device is alive and after it is destroyed alike.

issues.title: audio.h and AUDIO.md call cna_dynamic_sound_effect_instance_submit_buffer safe from a producer thread, but every call off the creation thread returns CNA_RESULT_THREAD
issues.summary: The submission routes resolve the instance through HandleRegistry::Get, which refuses any thread other than the handle's creation thread, so the documented canonical producer-thread usage fails; AUDIO.md's own threading section states the stricter rule.
issues.public_contract: cna_dynamic_sound_effect_instance_submit_buffer, cna_dynamic_sound_effect_instance_submit_float_buffer_ext
issues.expected: The Doxygen of cna_dynamic_sound_effect_instance_submit_buffer in {{src:modules/c-api/include/CNA/C/audio.h|audio.h}} says copying the bytes “is what makes this route safe to call from a producer thread while playback runs, which is the canonical usage”; {{src:docs/c-api/AUDIO.md|AUDIO.md}} repeats it for streaming instances.
issues.actual:
Both routes in {{src:modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiAudio.cpp|CnaCApiAudio.cpp}} call BorrowDynamicInstance → GetSoundEffectInstance → HandleRegistry::Get, and Get in {{src:modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiDetail.hpp|CnaCApiDetail.hpp}} returns CNA_RESULT_THREAD whenever the calling thread is not the slot's creation thread. AUDIO.md's “Threads, hardware and shutdown” section says every audio call runs on the game creation thread, so the documents contradict each other and the code follows the stricter statement.

Since C ABI 0.39.0 (CBIND-141) a game can opt in with cna_game_set_foreign_thread_calls_ext(game, CNA_TRUE): a call another thread's handle refused is then queued for the game thread, and the producer blocks until Update/Draw or cna_game_run_foreign_thread_calls_ext serves it. The switch is off by default, so the documented producer-thread call still returns CNA_RESULT_THREAD; with it on, submission is serialized through the game thread rather than made concurrently with playback. CBIND-154 (ABI 0.43.0) lifted the creating-thread rule only for cna_sound_effect_play and cna_sound_effect_play_with_settings; the submission routes keep it.

issues.title: GraphicsRendererSelection::IsLatched() is documented to latch when the first GraphicsDevice begins construction; it latches only on successful resolution
issues.summary: The header comment on IsLatched() says the selection latches when the first GraphicsDevice begins construction, but GraphicsDevice::resolveRenderer latches only after a renderer has been created, so a resolution that fails before any renderer exists leaves the choice open. (A constructor that fails after resolution has already latched: CNA-BUG-095.)
issues.public_contract: CNA::GraphicsRendererSelection::IsLatched() as documented in CNA/GraphicsRendererSelection.hpp
issues.expected: The implemented and intended rule, stated in the design note beside the latch call (RTR-P5-18) and in the C header's wording for cna_graphics_renderer_get_is_latched_ext ("once a renderer has been created"): the selection latches when a renderer has been successfully created, so a game whose GraphicsDevice resolution fails can reconfigure and try again.
issues.actual: The Doxygen comment on IsLatched() in {{src:modules/core/include/CNA/GraphicsRendererSelection.hpp|GraphicsRendererSelection.hpp}} says it "becomes true when the first GraphicsDevice begins construction"; its @brief, "Whether the selection can still be changed", is also inverted for a function that returns true once latched. GraphicsDevice::resolveRenderer in {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}} calls GraphicsRendererSelectionAccessEXT::Latch, the only production latch site, only after a candidate renderer has been created, and its comment explains that latching up front was the first design and was wrong. A reader of the header would conclude that a resolution that failed before creating any renderer froze the selection; it did not.

issues.title: docs/framework-design.md says the Framework.Design registration associates the twelve value types with ordered descriptor collections; registerConverter registers only converter factories
issues.summary: registerConverter registers only a TypeConverterAttribute for each of the twelve math types, while CNA's design note says the registration associates the types with converter factories and ordered descriptor collections. The ordered descriptors exist only inside each converter, so the sentence overstates what the registration does.
issues.public_contract: The registration described in docs/framework-design.md, and System::ComponentModel::TypeDescriptor::GetProperties for the XNA math value types
issues.expected: {{src:docs/framework-design.md|framework-design.md}} states that linking and using a Design header "pulls a once-only registration translation unit that associates all twelve XNA value types with converter factories and ordered descriptor collections". issues.title: docs/graphics-resource-lifetime.md says existing XNA resources hold a unique_ptr renderer and names a non-existent ITexture2DRenderer; Texture2D, Texture3D and TextureCube hold shared_ptr renderers and Texture2D's public copies share one
issues.summary: The document's Ownership Model gives unique_ptr renderer ownership for existing XNA resources, a list its scope sentence extends to Texture2D and RenderTarget2D, and knows only one kind of sharing: an internal record on non-copyable modern resources. Texture2D, Texture3D and TextureCube hold shared_ptr renderers, and Texture2D's public copies share the renderer and CPU shadow.

issues.expected: The lifetime document describes the ownership that the resource classes implement, so that a maintainer reasoning about disposal, copies and native-handle retention starts from the right model.
issues.actual: {{src:docs/graphics-resource-lifetime.md|graphics-resource-lifetime.md}} section 1 says existing XNA resources hold a std::unique_ptr<IXxxRenderer> (for example IVertexBufferRenderer or ITexture2DRenderer) and that a renderer may hand its native handles to an internal retained record that “is not a second public owner”; its scope sentence names Texture2D and RenderTarget2D among the covered types. At TARGET no type named ITexture2DRenderer exists under modules/ (the real interface is ITextureRenderer). {{src:modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Texture2D.hpp|Texture2D.hpp}} holds std::shared_ptr<ITextureRenderer> renderer_, a shared cpuPixels_ vector and shared extraMipLevels_; its public CNAEXT copy constructor and copy assignment (user-defined since af3c5037c so that every live copy registers with the device for disposal, as TextureCube's now do too) are documented as 'a second handle to the same texture' (shared until a full-level SetData, KF-4), and GetRendererWeak()/GetCpuPixelsWeak() hand out weak references. Texture3D.hpp and TextureCube.hpp hold std::shared_ptr renderers too. Of the five resource headers read, only VertexBuffer.hpp and IndexBuffer.hpp follow the unique-ownership rule, which is the shape section 5's move example uses. The document has no account of the texture family's public value-copy sharing.

issues.title: LocalNetworkGamer::SendData in a Local or LocalWithLeaderboards session silently drops every packet, so neither the sender nor another local gamer ever receives it
issues.summary: NetworkSession::Update raises PacketSend events only when real networking is enabled (SystemLink, or a service-backed PlayerMatch/Ranked session), so SendData in a Local or LocalWithLeaderboards session reports success and delivers nothing, although SendData is documented to reach every gamer in the session, the sender included.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::LocalNetworkGamer::SendData, ReceiveData and getIsDataAvailableProperty in a NetworkSession of type Local or LocalWithLeaderboards
issues.expected: XNA documents LocalNetworkGamer.SendData as sending to all gamers in a session ('This includes the gamer sending the packet') without any session-type qualifier, and describes Local sessions as making it easier to share code between local and online modes; the decompiled SendDataWorker queues every packet regardless of session type. CNA's own LocalNetworkGamer.hpp repeats 'every gamer in the session', no CNA document lists the non-delivery as a limitation, and CNA's CLAUDE.md says XNA wins over FNA where they disagree.
issues.actual: LocalNetworkGamer::SendData enqueues a PacketSend event; NetworkSession::Update in {{src:modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp|NetworkSession.cpp}} delivers it only when ENetBackend::RealNetworkingEnabled(sessionType_) (true for SystemLink alone, {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/ENetBackend.cpp|ENetBackend.cpp}}) or the session is a service-backed PlayerMatch/Ranked session, so in Local and LocalWithLeaderboards sessions the event is silently dropped, including a packet a local gamer sends to itself or to another local gamer. SendData reports nothing and IsDataAvailable stays false. The drop is deliberate FNA parity, pinned by LocalNetworkGamerTest.SendDataThenReceiveDataRoundtrip and NetworkSessionTypePolicyTest.SendDataStaysFullySyntheticForEverySyntheticType, a comment in Update now records the no-op on the premise that these sessions "have no remote gamers", which overlooks delivery between local gamers, and no CNA header documents it.

issues.title: A join beyond MaxGamers is not refused: the host sends ServerWelcome, AddRemoteGamer throws Session is full!, and the receive path's catch-all drops it, so the joiner never sees SessionFull
issues.summary: HandleClientHello sends ServerWelcome and registers wire ids before AddRemoteGamer checks capacity; the receive path swallows the exception, so an over-capacity client stays connected and NetworkSessionJoinError::SessionFull is never produced.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::NetworkSession::Join on a full host (ENetBackend HandleClientHello, NetworkSession::AddRemoteGamer, NetworkSessionJoinError::SessionFull)
issues.expected: A client that joins a session already holding MaxGamers gamers should be refused with a NetworkSessionJoinException carrying NetworkSessionJoinError::SessionFull, the value the XNA API defines for exactly this case, and the host's roster and the other peers should be left alone.
issues.actual: {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/ENetBackend.cpp|HandleClientHello}} rejects only a duplicate handshake and a join in progress that the host forbids. It then creates the joining client's NetworkGamer objects, assigns and registers their wire ids, sends ServerWelcome, and only afterwards calls {{src:modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp|NetworkSession::AddRemoteGamer}}, which throws InvalidOperationException(“Session is full!”) once allGamers_ has reached maxGamers_. The receive path wraps the whole message switch in a catch-all that drops the exception, so a bad packet cannot take down Update(). The over-capacity client therefore has been welcomed and stays connected with its wire ids registered, the gamers beyond the limit are never added to the host's roster or announced to the other peers, and the SystemLink path produces no SessionFull (only the online service binding, {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/OnlineSessionBinding.cpp|OnlineSessionBinding.cpp}}, throws it).

sources.note: HandleClientHello: no capacity check before ServerWelcome; the receive path catches std::exception
AddRemoteGamer throws Session is full! after allGamers_ reaches maxGamers_
the only place SessionFull is thrown, for service-backed sessions

issues.title: SoundEffect::Play(volume, pitch, pan) clamps pitch, does not check volume and returns false when disposed, where XNA 4.0 throws
issues.summary: XNA 4.0's SoundEffect.Play(float, float, float) throws ObjectDisposedException when disposed and ArgumentOutOfRangeException for volume or pitch out of range; CNA returns false when disposed, clamps pitch and passes volume through.
issues.public_contract: SoundEffect::Play(float volume, float pitch, float pan) and the C route cna_sound_effect_play_with_settings
issues.expected: XNA 4.0's SoundEffect.Play(float, float, float) (decompiled Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Audio.SoundEffect; read, not executed) throws ObjectDisposedException when the effect is disposed and assigns the arguments through the SoundEffectInstance Volume, Pitch and Pan setters, which throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException outside [0, 1], [-1, 1] and [-1, 1]. CNA's own SoundEffectInstance setters follow those ranges since KF-12 (49119a34c).
issues.actual: SoundEffect::Play(float, float, float) in {{src:modules/audio/src/Xna/SoundEffect.cpp|SoundEffect.cpp}} returns false for a disposed effect, range-checks only pan, clamps pitch to [-1, 1] (its comment: "Pitch is clamped rather than validated") and hands volume to the mixer track's gain without a check. So Play(1.0f, 5.0f, 0.0f) plays where XNA throws, a volume of 2 or -1 is accepted, and a call on a disposed effect is refused silently instead of raising. The same values on a SoundEffectInstance throw, so the two paths disagree. {{src:modules/c-api/include/CNA/C/audio.h|audio.h}} documents the C route cna_sound_effect_play_with_settings with the same asymmetry ("pan is range-checked and pitch is clamped").

issues.title: An XNB BoundingSphere or Model mesh sphere with a negative radius fails to load, although XNA and CNA's own XNB writer accept it
issues.summary: ContentReader::ReadBoundingSphere builds the sphere through the validating BoundingSphere(Vector3, float) constructor, so a negative radius in a .xnb throws System::ArgumentException, where XNA's reader assigns Center and Radius as stored.
issues.public_contract: ContentManager::Load of an .xnb holding a BoundingSphere (BoundingSphereReader) or a Model (the per-mesh bounding sphere)
issues.expected: XNA 4.0's ContentReader.ReadBoundingSphere reads the centre and the radius into the sphere's fields without a check, so content that stores a negative radius (a degenerate or hand-made asset) loads, and a Model's mesh bounds stay advisory. CNA's own XNB writer follows XNA here: it writes such a sphere rather than refusing it.
issues.actual: At this snapshot {{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentReader.cpp|ContentReader::ReadBoundingSphere}} returns BoundingSphere(center, radius), and since e1377c437 that constructor ({{src:modules/math/src/BoundingSphere.cpp|BoundingSphere.cpp}}) throws System::ArgumentException for a negative radius. The Model reader takes each mesh's sphere through the same call ({{src:modules/content/src/Xnb/XnbModelGraphReader.hpp|XnbModelGraphReader.hpp}}), so one negative mesh radius fails the whole model load. The writer side accepts the same value on purpose: the fuzz seed “a bounding sphere with a negative radius and a NaN centre” in {{src:modules/content/tests/CNA/Internal/Xnb/XnbWriterInputFuzzTests.cpp|XnbWriterInputFuzzTests.cpp}} expects Outcome::Written (“XNA writes the sphere the content gave it, and a Model's own bounds are advisory”), so a file CNA writes can be one CNA cannot read back.

issues.title: On FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver a TextureCube, Texture3D or mipmapped Texture2D changed between two draws of one frame shows its new contents in the earlier draw too
issues.summary: SDL_GPU and WEBGPU now order a texture upload after the queued draws that sample it, so SpriteSortMode::Immediate and other mid-frame SetData calls keep XNA's per-draw contents there; FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver still submits uploads ahead of the frame's draws and keeps the old contents only for a whole write of a single-level 2D texture.
issues.public_contract: Texture2D, TextureCube and Texture3D SetData between two draws of one frame (including two Draw calls of one SpriteSortMode::Immediate SpriteBatch) on the FNA3D renderer when FNA3D runs its SDL_GPU driver
issues.expected: XNA draws each call with the texture as it is at that call: a texture changed with SetData between two draws of one frame shows its old contents in the first draw and its new contents in the second. For SpriteSortMode::Immediate that means a texture changed between two Draw calls leaves the first sprite with the old contents.
issues.actual:
FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver (the libcna/FNA3D fork CNA pins in {{src:cmake/ThirdPartyFNA3D.cmake|ThirdPartyFNA3D.cmake}}, 10f650b9d0f6) records texture uploads on a command buffer of its own and submits it ahead of the frame's draws. SDLGPU_SetTextureData2D lets SDL cycle the texture, so that draws recorded earlier keep the old resource, only for a whole write of level 0 of a single-level, single-layer texture; SDLGPU_SetTextureDataCube and SDLGPU_SetTextureData3D never cycle. A TextureCube changed between two draws of one frame therefore shows its new contents in the earlier draw too: leg B of CNA's conformance program {{src:modules/graphics/examples/conformance/texture_setdata_after_draw_test.cpp|texture_setdata_after_draw}} fails on FNA3D (measured by CNA on 2026-10-24, SDL_GPU driver over Vulkan), and {{src:docs/fna3d-renderer.md|fna3d-renderer.md}} (“Texture upload ordering”) states that by the same source a Texture3D or a mipmapped Texture2D does the same. CNA treats this as the driver's behaviour, reported rather than worked around ({{src:handoff.md|handoff.md}} section 5.3). An Immediate SpriteBatch is affected only through such textures: CNA's FNA3D renderer flushes each Immediate sprite from Draw and uploads whole levels, so a single-level sprite texture keeps XNA's order, and leg B of {{src:modules/graphics/examples/spritebatch_sort_mode_semantics_test.cpp|spritebatch_sort_mode_semantics_test.cpp}} passes on FNA3D.

Fixed since first recorded: the entry was first published for CNA's own SDL_GPU and WEBGPU renderers, which replayed the sprites of an Immediate batch after a later upload. Since d9b513ee0 {{src:modules/renderers/sdl-gpu/src/SdlGpuRenderer.cpp|SdlGpuRenderer.cpp}} submits the queued work first when an upload reaches a Texture2D, TextureCube or Texture3D that a queued command still samples (SubmitQueuedSamplersEXT), and since d9b513ee0 and 96577db26 {{src:modules/renderers/webgpu/src/WebGPURenderer.cpp|WebGPURenderer.cpp}} writes such a texture into a fresh one and leaves the old one to the queued commands (RenameForWriteEXT, keyed on QueuedCycleEXT). Leg B of the sort-mode program now asserts XNA's red/blue instead of printing it, and CNA's handoff lists no open defect in section 5.1.

issues.title: FNA3D's Direct3D 11 driver cannot build some valid compiled effects: a ps_3_0 shader that reads two vertex outputs packed in one register fails to compile, and the integer input-layout rewrite can retype the wrong semantic
issues.summary: the MojoShader code behind FNA3D's Direct3D 11 driver, in CNA's pinned fork, names a struct member that does not exist when a ps_3_0 shader reads, from one register, semantics the vertex shader wrote to separate registers, so the generated HLSL fails to compile; and it finds the semantic of an integer vertex element by substring, so DEPTH1 can match an earlier DEPTH10 and swap their integer and float declarations.
issues.public_contract: Compiled XNA effects (Effect Framework bytecode) drawn on the FNA3D renderer when FNA3D runs its Direct3D 11 driver (Windows; FNA3D tries its SDL_GPU driver first, or the driver is selected with FNA3D_FORCE_DRIVER)
issues.expected: A compiled effect that Direct3D 9 runs should run on every FNA3D driver: a vertex shader may write the semantics a ps_3_0 pixel shader reads in any register layout, and an integer vertex element should change the declaration of exactly the semantic it names.
issues.actual: The FNA3D renderer builds FNA3D and MojoShader from CNA’s forks ({{src:cmake/ThirdPartyFNA3D.cmake|ThirdPartyFNA3D.cmake}}, MojoShader 03b686fe1a33). In that MojoShader, the code behind FNA3D's Direct3D 11 driver (mojoshader_d3d11.c) links a vertex shader’s output struct to the pixel shader’s input struct by name; when a ps_3_0 shader reads two semantics packed into one register (FOG in its x, TEXCOORD0 in yzw, both from v0) that the vertex shader wrote to separate registers (o1.x, o2.yzw), the generated HLSL names a member that does not exist and does not compile (R9-01; CNA records it as present before the review too). When the input layout has an integer element, the same file rewrites the declaration of its semantic in the HLSL source by locating <name><index> with strstr, so DEPTH1 is found inside an earlier DEPTH10 and the integer and float declarations of the two are swapped (R9-03). CNA lists both in {{src:handoff.md|handoff.md}} section 5.2 as found in the review’s third round and not fixed, and notes that CNA’s committed effects contain neither shape. The same section records that the rewrite looks for PSIZE0 where the generated HLSL writes PSIZE.

issues.origin: new finding at the 3b43bd86 pin move (Deep Dives review, confirmed by the coordinator): RendererFeature::MultiSampleMask (35, c7f6c68e5, CNA-DEMOS DC-R2) answers against what two renderer configurations do with a mask
issues.title: RendererFeature::MultiSampleMask misreports EasyGL without glSampleMaski (OPENGLES3 on an OpenGL ES 3.0 context, WEBGL2) and WEBGPU over wgpu-native's Metal driver
issues.summary: The feature is defined so that Unsupported means a mask has no effect and Supported means any mask is applied, but EasyGL without glSampleMaski answers Unsupported while it throws NotSupportedException for every mask other than all ones, and WEBGPU over wgpu-native's Metal driver answers Supported while it refuses a partial mask; a program that trusts the answer either fails at the draw or never learns that the mask is refused.

The answer should describe what the renderer then does.
issues.actual: {{src:modules/renderers/easygl/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/EasyGL/EasyGLRenderer.hpp|EasyGLRenderer.hpp}} answers Unsupported when the context has no glSampleMaski (desktop GL before 3.2, OpenGL ES 3.0, WebGL 2), but ApplyBlendState in {{src:modules/renderers/easygl/src/EasyGLRenderer.cpp|EasyGLRenderer.cpp}} throws NotSupportedException (“BlendState.MultiSampleMask requires desktop GL 3.2 or OpenGL ES 3.1”) for every mask other than all ones there, a mask of none included: the mask is not without effect, it is refused. {{src:modules/renderers/webgpu/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/WebGPU/WebGPURenderer.hpp|WebGPURenderer.hpp}} answers Supported whenever a device exists, while {{src:modules/renderers/webgpu/src/WebGPURenderer.cpp|WebGPURenderer.cpp}} (SupportsPartialMultiSampleMaskEXT, false on WGPUBackendType_Metal) refuses a partial mask on wgpu-native’s Metal driver, whose pipelines have no sample mask; by the definition above that is Restricted.

issues.title: CNA::Logger serialises writes but not level changes, and a sink must not call back into the logger
issues.summary: minimumLevel_ is read and written without synchronisation and the sink runs under a non-recursive mutex, so changing the level while other threads log is a data race and a sink that logs deadlocks; the header states neither limit.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Logger::SetMinimumLevel, GetMinimumLevel, Log and its helpers, SetSink and ResetSink
issues.expected: The header documents no thread-safety or re-entrancy rule. The implementation's own comment says the mutex exists so "two threads cannot interleave halves of a line", which invites concurrent use.
issues.actual:
• Logger::minimumLevel_ is a plain static LogLevel: SetMinimumLevel writes it and IsEnabled (called first in Log) reads it without the lock or an atomic, so changing the level while another thread logs is a data race (undefined behaviour in C++, benign on common targets).
  • Log calls the installed sink while holding SinkMutex(), a non-recursive std::mutex; a sink that logs through Logger, or calls SetSink or ResetSink, locks it again from the same thread, which is undefined behaviour and in practice a deadlock.
  • An exception thrown by a sink propagates to the caller of Log (the lock is released).

Concurrent Log calls themselves are safe: formatting happens before the lock and the write happens under it.

sources.note: Logger::Log, IsEnabled, SetMinimumLevel, SetSink, ResetSink, SinkMutex
the public API, with no thread or re-entrancy statement
eleven LoggerTest cases; none concurrent or re-entrant

issues.evidence: Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; nothing was built or executed for this entry. Both limits follow from the storage and locking in Logger.cpp. No thread-sanitizer run was made.
issues.reproduction:
Illustrative; not compiled or run for this entry.

CNA::Logger::SetSink([](CNA::LogLevel, CNA::LogCategory, std::string_view line) {
    if (line.size() > 200)
        CNA::Logger::Warn("long log line");   // re-enters Log while SinkMutex() is held: deadlock
});
CNA::Logger::Info(std::string(300, 'x'));
issues.tests_current: The eleven cases in {{src:modules/core/tests/CNA/LoggerTests.cpp|LoggerTests.cpp}} cover the level gate, every level and category reaching the sink, the conditional overloads, the line format, ResetSink, stderr rather than stdout, and the level round trip. None runs two threads or installs a re-entrant sink.
issues.regression_test: If the contract is widened: make minimumLevel_ atomic and add a thread-sanitizer test that logs from several threads while another changes the level; either call the sink outside the lock (copying it first) or reject re-entry, with a test for a sink that logs. If it is kept narrow, document both rules in Logger.hpp.
issues.blast_radius: Programs that change the level while other threads (renderer, audio or loader threads) log, and sinks that forward into code that itself logs through CNA::Logger. Single-threaded configuration at start-up and plain concurrent logging are unaffected.
issues.workaround: Set the minimum level before starting other threads, and write sinks that never call CNA::Logger, SetSink or ResetSink (queue the line and emit it after the sink returns).

issues.title: Game::ShowMissingRequirementMessage is a virtual hook that nothing in CNA calls
issues.summary: XNA 4.0's Game.Run catches NoSuitableGraphicsDeviceException and NoAudioHardwareException and offers them to ShowMissingRequirementMessage before rethrowing; CNA declares the virtual but Game::Run never invokes it, so an override has no effect.
issues.public_contract: virtual bool Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Game::ShowMissingRequirementMessage(const std::exception&)
issues.expected: In XNA 4.0 (IL of Game.RunGame) the two requirement exceptions are caught and passed to ShowMissingRequirementMessage; the default shows a host message, and the exception is rethrown only if it returns false.
issues.actual: CNA's implementation returns false and is referenced nowhere else: Game::Run in {{src:modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp|Game.cpp}} logs any escaping exception and rethrows it without consulting the hook, so an override is never called. Only exceptions raised inside Run can reach that handler (for example NoAudioHardwareException from SoundEffect or DynamicSoundEffectInstance during LoadContent). The NoSuitableGraphicsDeviceException throw sites read at 3b43bd86 (the UseNullDevice/UseReferenceDevice renderer requirement and the DirectX 9 HiDef shader-model check) run while a GraphicsDevice is constructed, which for Game's own device happens in Game's constructor, before Run exists; since a71cc2415 (CBIND-144) Game's constructor also converts every other failure to create its device into a NoSuitableGraphicsDeviceException (CreateGameGraphicsDevice), likewise before Run; a hook wired into Run alone would not see those.

issues.title: Sub-pixel SpriteBatch destinations reach only EasyGL and SOFTWARE; every other renderer truncates them to whole pixels
issues.summary: SpriteBatch forwards float destinations through ISpriteBatchRenderer's sub-pixel Draw overload, whose default truncates toward zero into an integer Rectangle; only the EasyGL and SOFTWARE sprite renderers override it.
issues.public_contract: SpriteBatch::Draw / DrawString with fractional positions or scales; ISpriteBatchRenderer::Draw(texture, float x, float y, float w, float h, ...)
issues.expected: XNA 4.0 carries sprite destinations as floats to the GPU, so a sprite at x = 10.5 lands between pixels and is filtered by the sampler (the interface comment in {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp|IGraphicsRenderer.hpp}} says the same).
issues.actual: SpriteBatch calls the float overload for every queued sprite ({{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/SpriteBatch.cpp|SpriteBatch.cpp}}). The default implementation quantises each value with static_cast<int> (truncation toward zero, so -0.5 becomes 0) and forwards to the integer-Rectangle overload. Only EasyGLSpriteBatchRenderer and the SOFTWARE sprite renderer override it; SDL_GPU, WEBGPU, DIRECTX9, FNA3D and the rest draw on whole pixels. Smooth sub-pixel scrolling and fractional text scaling therefore snap on those renderers.

issues.title: Several live GraphicsDevices share process-wide window and input slots with last-writer semantics
issues.summary: The window-to-renderer registry is a static, unsynchronised map with no ownership check, and TextInputEXT and Mouse keep one process-wide window slot, so two devices overwrite each other's registry entries and input target.

issues.title: Mirrored glTF placements keep the shared winding, so under the default cull mode they render back-facing
issues.summary: A placement whose world transform has a negative determinant is detected and reported (mirrored-winding-unapplied) but CNA neither reverses its winding nor changes cull state, and exposes no per-mesh flag for the application to do it.
issues.public_contract: ContentManager::Load<Model> on glTF files with negatively scaled or mirroring node transforms; Model::Draw
issues.expected: glTF §3.7.4 requires the front-face winding to be reversed when a node's global transform has a negative determinant, so mirrored geometry stays front-facing.
issues.actual: ContentManager.cpp logs, per mirrored placement, that CNA "does not reverse the triangle winding for it, so this placement's front faces are back-facing under the default cull mode", and GltfImportCore.cpp (AppendGltfInstanceReportEXT) records mirrored-winding-unapplied: "the application must reverse culling for this draw". The reason is architectural: the index and vertex buffers are shared with unmirrored placements of the same mesh, and cull state is per-draw device state. No public Model or ModelMesh property carries a per-mesh mirroring flag. The only public route is the Model's import report (Model::getGltfImportReportEXTProperty), which lists each mirrored placement by node name in a diagnostic whose Code is mirrored-winding-unapplied, so an application has to map that node name to the ModelMesh it draws, or recompute the determinant from the bone transforms.

issues.title: CUBICSPLINE bone and node channels are replayed linearly between samples taken at least every 1/60 s, an approximation of the authored curve
issues.summary: BuildTrack samples each CUBICSPLINE interval at least every 1/60 s and AnimationPlayer lerps/slerps between the samples, so the curve between samples is approximated.
issues.public_contract: AnimationPlayer and SkinnedModelEXT playback of glTF clips with CUBICSPLINE interpolation
issues.expected: glTF CUBICSPLINE channels define a Hermite curve between keys, which a player is expected to evaluate.
issues.actual:
BuildTrack in {{src:modules/content/src/GltfImport/GltfImportCore.cpp|GltfImportCore.cpp}} resamples a bone's channels onto the union of their key times and, since a9d378c06, also samples every CUBICSPLINE interval at least every 1/60 s (four samples at the least) and adds a hold key 10 µs before each STEP key, each evaluated with the channel's own mode. SampleTrack in {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/AnimationPlayer.cpp|AnimationPlayer.cpp}} still interpolates linearly (Slerp for rotation) between those samples, so a CUBICSPLINE curve is piecewise-linear between samples rather than evaluated. {{src:docs/gltf-limitations.md|gltf-limitations.md}} records the result: anim-cubicspline plays within 0.0021 units of its spline (it was 0.962 off), “a bound for that fixture, not a universal one, because authored tangents may bend a spline more sharply”. Morph-weight tracks keep their tangents and are evaluated as Hermite curves.

The dense sampling is CNA's fix for CNA-DEMOS-ISSUE-031 (STEP and CUBICSPLINE playing as LINEAR), which CNA closed on a complete checkpoint (6c8b042c4, 2026-10-24); the approximation between samples is what remains.

issues.title: XACT features FAudio never finished are unimplemented: QUEUE and REPLACE_QUIETEST limits, band-pass track filters, reverb sends and DSP-preset RPCs
issues.summary: CNA reproduces FAudio's shipped behaviour: QUEUE and REPLACE_QUIETEST evict the oldest cue, a cue-level limit picks its victim from the whole bank, band-pass filters cannot be decoded, and reverb and DSP-preset RPC targets do nothing.
issues.public_contract: AudioEngine category and cue instance limits; XACT sound-bank track filters; Cue RPC evaluation; SoundEffectInstance reverb
issues.expected: XACT defines FAIL, QUEUE, REPLACE_OLDEST, REPLACE_QUIETEST and REPLACE_LOWEST_PRIORITY instance-limit behaviours, per-track low-, high- and band-pass filters, a reverb send and DSP-preset RPC parameters.
issues.actual: CheckCategoryInstanceLimit and CheckCueInstanceLimit in {{src:modules/audio/src/Xna/AudioEngine.cpp|AudioEngine.cpp}} treat QUEUE and REPLACE_QUIETEST as REPLACE_OLDEST and, for a cue-level limit, search every live cue of the bank for the victim, matching FAudio's handle_instance_limit (whose own source carries a FIXME). {{src:modules/audio/src/Internal/XactParser.cpp|XactParser.cpp}} decodes the filter type with FAudio's (filterData >> 1) & 0x02, which can yield only low- or high-pass. Cue::EvaluateRpc in {{src:modules/audio/src/Xna/Cue.cpp|Cue.cpp}} applies RPC targets 0 (volume), 1 (pitch), 3 (filter frequency) and 4 (filter Q) only: the reverb-send target (parameter 2) and every DSP-preset target (parameter 5 and above) are parsed but never applied, and SoundEffectInstance::INTERNAL_applyReverb is a documented no-op because the mixer has no aux-send bus. CHECKLIST.md records the instance-limit collapse, the low/high-only filter decode, the DSP-preset RPC gap and the reverb no-op as accepted deviations, and the dated audio plan that recorded the unapplied reverb-send RPC target (P10-RPC-001) was deleted on 2026-10-11 (96c6e77be) without the record moving elsewhere.
