issues.title: TerminalSession does not restore or re-establish the terminal on job-control stop and continue (SIGTSTP/SIGCONT)
issues.summary: The session's restoring signal set covers termination and crash signals but not SIGTSTP/SIGCONT, so a Ctrl-Z that suspends a terminal game leaves the terminal in raw mode, the alternate screen and mouse reporting until the process is resumed.
issues.public_contract: CNA::Platform::Terminal::TerminalSession terminal restoration on job-control signals
issues.expected: The session's whole purpose is that a terminal game never leaves the user with a broken terminal: it restores on normal exit, on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGQUIT, on SIGABRT and the hard-crash signals, and on an uncaught exception. Job-control suspend (Ctrl-Z → SIGTSTP) leaves the process alive but stopped, with the terminal still owned; a robust interactive terminal program restores cooked mode and the main screen while suspended and re-enters its session on SIGCONT.
issues.actual: {{src:modules/platform/src/Terminal/TerminalSession.cpp|kRestoringSignals}} is {SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT, SIGABRT, SIGSEGV, SIGBUS, SIGFPE, SIGILL}. SIGTSTP and SIGCONT are absent, and raw mode clears ISIG, so the terminal driver will not even generate SIGTSTP from Ctrl-Z while the game runs; a SIGTSTP sent to the process group by other means stops the process with the alternate screen up, the cursor hidden, mouse reporting on and the line discipline in raw mode. The shell that regains the foreground sees that state until the game is continued.

sources.note: kRestoringSignals (no SIGTSTP/SIGCONT); raw mode clears ISIG

issues.evidence: Checked by reading TerminalSession.cpp's signal set and raw-mode setup at 3b43bd86. Not executed. The Development terminal page states the limit explicitly (“SIGTSTP and SIGCONT are not in the restoring set”), and CNA's own terminal feasibility analysis lists the restoration signals without SIGTSTP, so this is a scoped, currently-unimplemented behaviour rather than a contradiction of a stated contract.
issues.tests_current: {{src:modules/platform/tests/CNA/Platform/TerminalRestorationTests.cpp|TerminalRestorationTests.cpp}} drives the restoring signals and the forced-exit limit; no case covers suspend/continue.
issues.regression_test: A pseudo-terminal harness that sends SIGTSTP to a session, checks the terminal is restored to cooked mode and the main screen while stopped, sends SIGCONT, and checks the session's prologue is re-emitted.
issues.blast_radius: Interactive terminal games suspended by job control (mainly where something sends SIGTSTP, since raw mode disables the Ctrl-Z keystroke path). The termination and crash paths are handled.
issues.workaround: Resume the game (fg) to restore the terminal; avoid suspending a running terminal game.

issues.title: A fixed-step TargetElapsedTime above 500 ms never produces an Update from Game::Tick, essentially the same ceiling XNA 4.0 has
issues.summary: With IsFixedTimeStep true, Game::Tick clamps the accumulator to MaxElapsedTime (500 ms) before its update loop, so a TargetElapsedTime above 500 ms is never reached: Update does not run while Draw keeps running, at about 1 / (target - 500 ms) per second (twice a second for a one-second target). XNA 4.0's Tick has essentially the same ceiling (about 508 ms, because of its 1/64 snap), but neither updates nor draws above it, so the limit is inherited; the setter accepts such a value silently.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Game::setTargetElapsedTimeProperty(const System::TimeSpan&) with IsFixedTimeStep true; Game::Tick()
issues.expected: Microsoft's documentation says a fixed-step Game tries to call Update on the interval in TargetElapsedTime, and the setter rejects only zero and negative values (as CNA's does), so a one-second target might be expected to update once a second. Neither XNA 4.0 nor CNA delivers that: the effective contract is a target of at most about 500 ms. CNA's Game.hpp documents only 'positive and non-zero'.
issues.actual: Game::Tick waits until accumulatedElapsedTime_ reaches TargetElapsedTime_, polls events, then clamps the accumulator to MaxElapsedTime (500 ms); the update loop 'while accumulated >= TargetElapsedTime_' therefore never runs for a target above 500 ms, stepCount stays zero, and the tick still draws, about twice a second. XNA 4.0 (IL of Game.Tick and GameClock) clamps the per-tick elapsed time to 500 ms, snaps an elapsed value within 1/64 of the target to the target, divides the sum with its leftover accumulator by the target and, when the quotient is zero, returns before GameClock.AdvanceFrameTime and before storing the sum, so its accumulator never reaches a target above about 508 ms and it neither updates nor draws. The difference is that CNA keeps drawing and that a target between 500 and 508 ms works in XNA only.

issues.title: WEBGPU does not propagate a real device loss: OnDeviceLost only logs, so DeviceLost, the device status and the draw gate react only to the debug hooks
issues.summary: WebGPURenderer sets its lost flag, closes CanBeginDrawEXT() and raises DeviceLost only inside DebugSimulateContextLoss; the callback registered for a real loss only writes to stderr. CNA's own plan (WEBGPU-182) records the driver-reported path as not done and unverified, so this is an incomplete feature rather than a broken contract.
issues.public_contract: GraphicsDevice::DeviceLost / DeviceReset, getGraphicsDeviceStatusProperty() and the CanBeginDrawEXT() gate behind GraphicsDeviceManager::BeginDraw, on the WEBGPU renderer
issues.expected: XNA raises DeviceLost and reports GraphicsDeviceStatus::Lost when the device is lost, and DirectX 9, 11 and 12 and Vulkan raise it from their real error paths through GraphicsRendererCreateArgs::deviceEventCallback. That channel is opt-in, though, and for WEBGPU nothing documented promises a real loss reaches it: {{src:docs/webgpu-renderer.md|webgpu-renderer.md}} describes recovery through the debug hooks only, and {{src:plans/plan_webgpu.md|plan_webgpu.md}} WEBGPU-182 closes with 'what is NOT done is the driver-reported path'. The same document adds a WebGPU-specific rule: a lost device must be gated before the acquire, because wgpuSurfaceGetCurrentTexture on a surface whose device is lost panics inside wgpu-native and aborts the process, and CanBeginDrawEXT() returning false is what stands between a lost device and that abort.
issues.actual: RequestDeviceOnlyEXT (also reached through RequestAdapterAndDevice) registers the free function OnDeviceLost as deviceLostCallbackInfo.callback with no user data. OnDeviceLost prints "CNA WebGPU device lost (...)" to stderr and does nothing else; without a renderer pointer it cannot set deviceLost_, raise RendererDeviceEvent::Lost or close CanBeginDrawEXT() (which returns !deviceLost_). The only code that does those things is WebGPURenderer::DebugSimulateContextLoss, and the only recovery is DebugRestoreContext; both are debug hooks the renderer never calls itself. When a real loss reaches the callback, the game receives no DeviceLost, GraphicsDeviceStatus stays Normal, BeginDraw keeps returning true and the renderer continues its frame loop against the lost device; nothing rebuilds it. The header comment of DebugSimulateContextLoss says the callback 'stays wired for a real driver-reported loss', which overstates what the callback does.

issues.title: The renderer capability profile has no feature for pre-compiled SPIR-V payloads, so SDL_GPU reports every source-dialect feature Unsupported
issues.summary: BuildRendererCapabilityProfileEXT maps a renderer's declared dialect onto six source-dialect features. SDL_GPU declares SpirV, which CNA documents as compiled bytecode rather than source, so all six read Unsupported and no profile entry says a SPIR-V payload is accepted.
issues.public_contract: CNA::RendererCapabilityProfile ShaderDialect* features (GraphicsDevice::GetRendererCapabilityProfileEXT)
issues.expected: The RendererFeature ShaderDialect* entries are documented as 'Source-based effects consume ...', and ShaderDialectEXT::SpirV as 'Already-compiled SPIR-V bytecode, not Vulkan GLSL source text'. The profile exists so that a caller can choose a payload without trying it; for a bytecode-consuming renderer the machine-readable profile cannot say which payload it takes.
issues.actual: BuildRendererCapabilityProfileEXT in {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}} sets ShaderDialectGlslDesktop/GlslEs/GlslVulkan/Hlsl/Msl/Wgsl to supported only when ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() is true and the declared dialect equals that enumerator. SDL_GPU declares ShaderDialectEXT::SpirV, for which no feature exists ({{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/RendererCapabilityProfile.hpp|RendererCapabilityProfile.hpp}}), so all six read Unsupported. This is deliberate: {{src:modules/renderers/sdl-gpu/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/SdlGpu/SdlGpuRenderer.hpp|SdlGpuRenderer.hpp}} says GLSL is not claimed even in a libshaderc build, because that route compiles Vulkan-rule GLSL, where GLSL ES 3.00 is not a legal input. SDL_GPU answers ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT() true whenever a device exists, so its profile shows source execution supported with no source dialect. A caller must ask GraphicsDevice::SupportsShaderLanguageEXT(SpirV, stage) instead.

issues.title: A runtime .cnj Texture2D colorKey leaves keyed texels as straight-alpha (key RGB, alpha 0), so they are invisible only under a non-premultiplied blend state
issues.summary: The loose-tier .cnj Texture2D reader writes Color(keyR, keyG, keyB, 0) into a straight-alpha texture, deliberately: plans/plan_cnj.md CNB-9 defines the result as transparent with alpha 0, and CnjSourceFileTests pins it. Under SpriteBatch's default premultiplied AlphaBlend such a texel adds the key colour instead of vanishing; the compiled route premultiplies after keying and clears it.
issues.public_contract: ContentManager::Load<Texture2D>(name) for a .cnj Texture2D document with colorKey; SpriteBatch::Begin() default BlendState::AlphaBlend
issues.expected: A colour-keyed texel is not visible when the texture is drawn with SpriteBatch::Begin()'s default blend state, as it is when the same document is compiled to .cnb.
issues.actual: ApplyColorKey in {{src:modules/content/src/Xna/BuiltinContentLoaders.cpp|BuiltinContentLoaders.cpp}}, which the .cnj Texture2D reader in {{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentTexture2DLoaders.cpp|ContentTexture2DLoaders.cpp}} calls, replaces each matching texel with Color(keyR, keyG, keyB, 0) and does not premultiply; the texture is straight alpha like every loose-loaded image. BlendState::AlphaBlend (One, InverseSourceAlpha) then adds the key colour to the destination inside the sprite's rectangle. BlendState::NonPremultiplied hides the texel. The pipeline comment in {{src:modules/content/src/Pipeline/Texture2DContentPipeline.cpp|Texture2DContentPipeline.cpp}} records that an authored key keeps its colour on purpose.

issues.title: ScrollWheelValue drops sub-notch wheel motion: the SDL3 platform counts whole notches only, where XNA accumulates raw wheel units
issues.summary: The SDL3 platform truncates every wheel event to whole notches before scaling by 120 (a deliberate FNA-parity rule in docs/input-fna-fidelity.md), so high-resolution wheels and touchpads can scroll without changing ScrollWheelValue; XNA accumulates 1/120 units.
issues.public_contract: MouseState::getScrollWheelValueProperty() and getHorizontalScrollWheelValueEXTProperty() as reported by Mouse::GetState()
issues.expected: XNA 4.0 on Windows adds the raw signed WM_MOUSEWHEEL delta to the wheel value (MouseMessageHooker.WndProc, decompiled reference), so a high-resolution wheel moves it in steps smaller than 120. The SDL3 backend deliberately follows FNA instead (cast to int before multiplying by 120), which is the documented and tested behaviour; the contract on SDL3 is whole notches.
issues.actual:
{{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3EventMapper.cpp|Sdl3EventMapper.cpp}} passes SDL's float wheel.x/wheel.y, and AccumulateWheel in {{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3InputServices.cpp|Sdl3InputServices.cpp}} converts each event to an integer number of notches before multiplying by 120. An event of 0.25 notch adds nothing, so a touchpad or smooth-scrolling wheel that reports fractions per event can leave ScrollWheelValue unchanged for a whole gesture. SDL delivers the fractional amounts and CNA discards them, so this is a narrower contract on CNA's side, not a host constraint.

{{src:docs/input-fna-fidelity.md|input-fna-fidelity.md}} records the truncation as an intentional FNA match that keeps the value “a clean multiple of 120 exactly like XNA”; XNA's own hook does not truncate.

issues.title: NetworkSession's Local, LocalWithLeaderboards and SystemLink Begin/End pairs are synchronous: Begin runs the callback and returns a completed result, and End does the work on the caller's thread
issues.summary: For Local, LocalWithLeaderboards and SystemLink sessions, BeginCreate, BeginFind and BeginJoin run the callback inline and return a completed result; End* then blocks: 150 ms for a SystemLink Find, up to 5 s for a SystemLink Join.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::NetworkSession::BeginCreate/BeginFind/BeginJoin and the matching End* methods for Local, LocalWithLeaderboards and SystemLink sessions
issues.expected: XNA 4.0 (read from the decompiled Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Net assembly and its async dispatcher; not executed) registers each Begin* operation as pending: IsCompleted stays false until a dispatcher thread finishes it, the wait handle is signalled then, the AsyncCallback is queued to the thread pool, and End* returns the finished result.
issues.actual: In {{src:modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp|NetworkSession.cpp}} a NetworkSessionAction starts complete (IsCompleted true, wait handle signalled, CompletedSynchronously true). For every session type except PlayerMatch and Ranked, BeginCreate, BeginFind and BeginJoin invoke the AsyncCallback inline (InvokeActiveActionCallback) before returning. The work then runs in End* on the caller's thread. On native builds, EndFind waits the fixed 150 ms SystemLink discovery window, and EndJoin pumps the joined session for up to 5 s until the host's welcome arrives. A game that polls IsCompleted every frame and calls End* when it turns true therefore stalls there. Service-backed PlayerMatch/Ranked Create, Find and Join, and BeginJoinInvited, are genuinely pending (QueueOnlineSession, QueueServiceSearch): IsCompleted stays false until the CNA service answers, so they are not part of this entry.

issues.title: Only EasyGL leases its context to other threads: on every other renderer, graphics resources created on a loading thread have no CNA-level exclusion against the frame
issues.summary: GraphicsDevice's resource registry is now locked and EasyGL leases its context to resource creation on any thread, but every other renderer returns no lease and has no synchronization of its own, while XNA 4.0 creates its device D3DCREATE_MULTITHREADED.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Graphics::GraphicsDevice and GraphicsResource: creating or disposing resources from a thread other than the game thread
issues.expected: XNA 4.0 creates its Direct3D 9 device with D3DCREATE_MULTITHREADED (decompiled GraphicsDevice.CreateDevice sets creation flags 38, which is 0x26 and includes 0x4), so a loading thread can create textures and buffers while the game thread runs, and the game thread may wait for that thread. {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/RendererThreadContextLease.hpp|RendererThreadContextLease.hpp}} says renderer families that return no lease 'support concurrent resource creation directly or own a different synchronization boundary'.
issues.actual:
GraphicsDevice's resource registry is locked: AddResourceReference, RemoveResourceReference and TransferResourceReference take resourcesMutex_ ({{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}}, KF-1a). On EasyGL, resource construction, SetData, GetData and Dispose of textures, render targets, vertex and index buffers take the renderer's context lease on whatever thread they run ({{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsResource.cpp|GraphicsResource.cpp}}, LeaseRendererContext, KF-1), ContentReader holds it for a whole asset, and the game thread holds it for Initialize, BeginRun, every Tick and EndRun ({{src:modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp|Game.cpp}}, AcquireGameThreadContextLease, KF-16), so a loading thread works between frames. Only EasyGLRenderer implements AcquireThreadContextLeaseEXT; SDL_GPU, WEBGPU, DIRECTX9, FNA3D and SOFTWARE return no lease, and their sources hold no lock for it (SDL_GPU's only mutexes guard its queued buffer uploads and its shader-cross session). The lease contract nevertheless still claims that lease-less renderers 'support concurrent resource creation directly or own a different synchronization boundary'. On EasyGL itself, a game thread that waits inside LoadContent, Update or Draw for a thread that is creating graphics resources deadlocks, because it still holds the context ({{src:docs/opengl33-renderer.md|opengl33-renderer.md}}); XNA 4.0 allows that wait.

Fixed since first recorded: the registry lock (KF-1a) and the EasyGL lease on resource construction, data transfer and disposal (KF-1, 00b9c9898) and on the whole frame (KF-16, a033a9184); native device construction and teardown are serialized (BINDFIX-050, 5b4edd6cc).

issues.title: SDL_GPU honours BlendState.MultiSampleMask only as all-or-none and refuses a partial mask, and FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver ignores it, because SDL_gpu reserves its sample-mask fields
issues.summary: SDL 3.5.0 still documents SDL_GPUMultisampleState::sample_mask/enable_mask as reserved, so on a multisampled target SDL_GPU draws normally for a mask keeping every sample, drops the draw for a mask keeping none and throws NotSupportedException for any other; FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver writes the reserved field without effect. RendererFeature::MultiSampleMask reports both.
issues.public_contract: BlendState.MultiSampleMask / GraphicsDevice.MultiSampleMask on SDL_GPU and on the FNA3D renderer's SDL_GPU driver
issues.expected: XNA's HiDef profile restricts a draw to the samples a partial MultiSampleMask keeps. A renderer that cannot should say so: refuse the mask and report the boundary through its capabilities.
issues.actual:
SDL 3.5.0, the revision CNA pins (86296ac8), still documents SDL_GPUMultisampleState::sample_mask and enable_mask as reserved (“must be set to 0” / “false”). Since c7f6c68e5 (CNA-DEMOS DC-R2, on the owner's decision) {{src:modules/renderers/sdl-gpu/src/SdlGpuRenderer.cpp|SdlGpuRenderer.cpp}} records the mask in ApplyBlendState and judges it for every queued draw in PushDrawOrder against the bound target: on a multisampled target a mask that keeps every sample draws as before, one that keeps none drops the draw (exact, since such a draw writes no colour, depth, stencil or occlusion sample), and any other throws System::NotSupportedException; a single-sample target ignores the mask, as in XNA. RendererFeature::MultiSampleMask (C CNA_RENDERER_FEATURE_MULTI_SAMPLE_MASK) reports Restricted there. FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver writes the mask into the same reserved field, where it has no effect, so the FNA3D renderer reports the feature Supported on its OpenGL driver only ({{src:modules/renderers/fna3d/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Fna3d/Fna3dRenderer.hpp|Fna3dRenderer.hpp}}, MultiSampleMaskSupportEXT); on the SDL_GPU driver a partial mask is ignored without an exception. EasyGL (where the context has glSampleMaski), WEBGPU, SOFTWARE and DIRECTX9 report and apply arbitrary masks.

Narrowed since first recorded: SDL_GPU no longer drops the mask silently: masks keeping every sample or none are applied exactly, a partial mask is refused by name, and the support is queryable. CNA records the boundary in {{src:handoff.md|handoff.md}} section 5.2.

issues.title: EasyGL on GLES/WebGL contexts without GL_NV_polygon_mode or WEBGL_polygon_mode refuses most wireframe triangle draws
issues.summary: Without a polygon-mode extension EasyGL draws only two bounded stock routes as line loops (non-indexed PositionColor and indexed PositionNormal TriangleLists); every other FillMode::WireFrame triangle draw throws NotSupportedException.
issues.public_contract: RasterizerState.FillMode = WireFrame on the GLES and WebGL EasyGL profiles

issues.actual:
{{src:modules/renderers/easygl/src/EasyGLRenderer.cpp|EasyGLRenderer.cpp}}'s RequireSupportedFillModeEXT throws NotSupportedException for TriangleList/TriangleStrip draws when wireframe is requested and neither extension is present, with a message pointing at SupportsCapability(GraphicsCapability::WireFrame), unless the draw qualifies for one of two bounded stock routes that draw each triangle as a line loop. CanDrawStockWireframeAsLineLoops takes a single-stream, non-indexed VertexPositionColor TriangleList drawn with the stock effect, clipped in homogeneous space, with no culling, depth, stencil, scissor, bias, multisampling or render target. CanDrawStockIndexedWireframeAsLineLoops takes an indexed 24-byte VertexPositionNormal TriangleList with the stock lit program, keeping face culling and the depth test. TriangleStrip, other vertex layouts, custom, compiled, skinned or PBR effects, render targets, multisampling, scissor, stencil and depth bias still throw, and GraphicsCapability::WireFrame remains false.

issues.title: Android Compass and Motion: stopping waits at most five seconds for the sensor worker, after which the bridge is abandoned for good and a handler still running can outlive its owner
issues.summary: AndroidSensorBridge::Stop gives a wedged worker five seconds and then detaches it, marking the bridge permanently unable to start; a Compass or Motion destroyed after such a timeout, while a callback is still inside it, is an unsupported window.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Devices::Sensors::Compass and Motion on Android (AndroidCompassBackend and AndroidMotionBackend over Detail::AndroidSensorBridge): Start(), Stop(), Dispose() and destruction
issues.expected: Stopping or disposing a sensor returns once the native sensor queue has stopped delivering, a later Start() can use the sensor again, and destroying the owner never races a callback that is running inside it.
issues.actual: AndroidSensorBridge::Stop in {{src:modules/devices/src/Sensors/Detail/AndroidSensorBridge.cpp|AndroidSensorBridge.cpp}}, called from another thread, waits for the worker to finish for at most kNativeCallTimeout (five seconds). If Run() is stuck in ASensorManager_createEventQueue or ASensorEventQueue_enableSensor, or a handler blocks that long, Stop detaches the thread and sets abandoned_, which is never reset: every later Start() on that bridge returns false, and the abandoned native call cannot be cancelled. Compass::Dispose(bool) and Motion::Dispose(bool) null the owner in the SensorOwnerControlBlock first, so callbacks that have not yet passed their owner check do nothing; but {{src:modules/devices/include/Microsoft/Devices/Sensors/Detail/SensorOwnerControlBlock.hpp|SensorOwnerControlBlock.hpp}} documents as an accepted boundary that a callback which already passed the check and is running inside the owner is not protected against another thread completing the owner's destruction. Because Stop normally waits for the worker, that window opens when the bounded wait expires.

issues.summary: Threaded Emscripten builds default to WasmFS, which cannot link IDBFS, so StorageDevice there reports StorageDeviceNotConnectedException instead of persisting saves unless the application configures CNA_EMSCRIPTEN_USE_WASMFS=OFF.

issues.title: Under Emscripten, SystemLink discovery is empty, hosting binds the fixed port 61191 and Join returns before the handshake
issues.summary: The web build stubs out discovery (Find returns nothing), hosts on a fixed port only a Node.js relay can use, rebuilds a joining session as an outbound-only client and returns from Join before the server welcome; Node.js-run unit tests cover discovery and loopback handshakes, but no browser or two-process test exists.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::NetworkSession Create, Find, Join and Update for NetworkSessionType::SystemLink in Emscripten builds
issues.expected: A program that finds a LAN session, joins it and sends its first packet behaves the same on every target, or the target states what it cannot do.
issues.actual: The __EMSCRIPTEN__ branch of {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/ENetDiscoveryService.cpp|ENetDiscoveryService.cpp}} defines RegisterHost, UnregisterHost and Poll as empty functions and FindSessions as returning an empty vector, so Find always returns nothing on the web: "cannot search", not "no hosts". ENetBackend::StartHosting binds kEmscriptenHostPort (61191) instead of an OS-assigned port, because Emscripten's socket layer does not report the bound port back; only a Node.js-run relay or server can accept on it, since a browser tab cannot listen. ENetBackend::ConnectToHost replaces the session's transport state with an outbound-only client. EndJoin's bounded wait for the ServerWelcome is inside #ifndef __EMSCRIPTEN__ in {{src:modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp|NetworkSession.cpp}}, so Join returns while the construction-time local placeholder is still the host, and a caller that sends at once addresses itself until Update has processed the welcome. The networking demos and the process-spawning tests are excluded from Emscripten builds.

issues.title: Online PlayerMatch and Ranked session traffic needs a libcurl with WebSocket support; with macOS's system libcurl the relay refuses with RELAY_SECURE_WEBSOCKET_UNAVAILABLE
issues.summary: PlayerMatch and Ranked sessions carry their traffic over a WSS relay through libcurl's WebSocket API, so a libcurl without ws/wss and TLS (Apple's system libcurl 8.7.1, or one older than 7.86) refuses the relay and those sessions cannot run.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::NetworkSession Create, Join and JoinInvited for NetworkSessionType::PlayerMatch and Ranked with a configured CNA gamer-services endpoint; the realtime relay at /cna/relay/v1 and the push channel /cna/v1/events
issues.expected: Once a CNA gamer-services endpoint is configured, online PlayerMatch and Ranked sessions work on every desktop host CNA builds for, as they do on Linux.
issues.actual: Online session traffic (game data, voice, readiness) travels between machines through the service's authenticated WSS datagram relay, which CNA reaches through libcurl's WebSocket API (curl_ws_send/curl_ws_recv). Before it authenticates, {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/RelayWebSocket.cpp|RelayWebSocket.cpp}} checks the linked libcurl with relayTransportRefusal(): relayTransportRefusalFor refuses with RELAY_SECURE_WEBSOCKET_UNAVAILABLE unless the version is at least 7.86.0, its protocol list offers both ws and wss, and it has a TLS backend. Apple's system libcurl 8.7.1, which a macOS build links unless another curl is found, has no WebSocket support, so on such a build the relay never connects; the online session cannot become ready and, by reading {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/ServiceENetSession.cpp|ServiceENetSession.cpp}}, ends with a relay failure once its 15-second relay-recovery window has passed. The account's push channel (/cna/v1/events) uses the same libcurl WebSocket API in {{src:modules/gamer-services/src/Internal/GamerServicesBackend.cpp|GamerServicesBackend.cpp}}; without it the hints never arrive and the client falls back to its ordinary polling (invitations and parties every 5 seconds, messages and friends every 15). Sign-in, profiles, achievements, leaderboards, the session directory and SystemLink sessions do not use WebSockets and are unaffected. Before 14f74e81f the same build reported a misleading RELAY_CONFIGURATION instead of this refusal.

The capability rule is pinned by RelayTransportTest.RefusalNeedsWsAndWssWithTlsFromCurl7860 on synthetic version data (8.11 and 7.86.0 with ws/wss and TLS accepted; 7.85, Apple's 8.7.1 protocol list, ws without wss, no TLS and no protocol list refused). CNA's own record states the platform consequence: {{src:plans/plan_apple_m4.md|plan_apple_m4.md}} AM4-044 records the owner decision that with the system libcurl the relay cannot work on macOS and that Homebrew curl 8.22 has ws/wss, and {{src:docs/apple-platforms.md|apple-platforms.md}} records that a CNA build linking the SDK's libcurl 8.7.1 refuses the relay transport by name, so the server's harness-driven tests on the Mac needed a tree that found Homebrew curl. How the failure reaches a game (the relay-recovery window, then the session's failure code) was established by reading only. Which libcurl a given Linux distribution ships with WebSockets enabled was not surveyed; WebSockets became a default libcurl feature only in 8.11.

No test runs an online session against a libcurl without WebSockets end to end.
issues.regression_test: None needed for the rule itself; a configure-time check that warns when networking is enabled against a libcurl lacking ws/wss would surface the limitation at build time instead of at the first online session.
issues.blast_radius: Games that use online PlayerMatch or Ranked sessions (and their voice) in builds linked against a libcurl without WebSocket support, notably macOS builds that link the system libcurl; push hints in such builds degrade to polling. Local, LocalWithLeaderboards and SystemLink sessions and the non-realtime gamer services are unaffected. iOS builds currently disable networking altogether, and an Android build without a target libcurl refuses the service as a browser does (CNA records both separately).
issues.workaround: Build against a libcurl that offers ws and wss with TLS, for example Homebrew curl on macOS, so that CMake finds it before the system library.

issues.origin: new finding at the 3b43bd86 pin move: handoff.md section 5.2 newly lists FNA3D-MISSING-STOCK-INPUT for PbrEffect and SkinnedPbrEffect (measured by the museum's rv-shading on 2026-10-25); the refusal itself dates from 84bf6fc4a (AM4-190)
issues.title: FNA3D refuses a PbrEffect or SkinnedPbrEffect draw whose vertex declaration has no Tangent0 on its SDL_GPU and Direct3D 11 drivers, where every other renderer draws it with a neutral tangent
issues.summary: FNA3D's SDL_GPU and Direct3D 11 drivers cannot build a pipeline for a shader input the declaration lacks, so the FNA3D renderer throws NotSupportedException (FNA3D-MISSING-STOCK-INPUT) for a PBR draw over tangent-free vertices such as VertexPositionNormalTexture; its OpenGL driver and the other renderers supply a neutral tangent.
issues.public_contract: PbrEffect and SkinnedPbrEffect (CNAEXT) draws on the FNA3D renderer with a VertexDeclaration that has no Tangent element at usage index 0, when FNA3D runs its SDL_GPU or Direct3D 11 driver
issues.expected: Since 91612a0a3 (museum rv-shading, 2026-10-22) CNA's PBR effects do not depend on whether a mesh stores a tangent: a renderer supplies the neutral tangent the GL path reads for an absent input, and {{src:modules/graphics/examples/pbr_vertex_contract_test.cpp|pbr_vertex_contract_test.cpp}} draws the same surface from VertexPositionNormalTexture and from VertexPositionNormalTangentTexture. A tangent-free mesh should draw the same on every renderer that ships PbrEffect.
issues.actual: Before it binds the vertex buffers of a stock draw, {{src:modules/renderers/fna3d/src/Fna3dDraw.cpp|Fna3dDraw.cpp}} checks that every input the selected effect variant reads is declared (RequireStockVertexInputsDeclared); for CnaPbrEffect and CnaSkinnedPbrEffect that includes Tangent0. A missing input throws System::NotSupportedException (“FNA3D renderer (FNA3D-MISSING-STOCK-INPUT): ... FNA3D's SDL_GPU and Direct3D 11 drivers cannot create a pipeline for it (only its OpenGL driver reads a default for a missing input)”). The check is skipped only where the driver reads a default, which {{src:modules/renderers/fna3d/src/Fna3dRenderer.cpp|Fna3dRenderer.cpp}} records for FNA3D's OpenGL driver alone (driverDefaultsMissingVertexInputs_). FNA3D tries its SDL_GPU driver first ({{src:docs/fna3d-renderer.md|fna3d-renderer.md}}), so on a default FNA3D device a PBR draw over a tangent-free declaration, such as XNA's VertexPositionNormalTexture, throws, where FNA3D's OpenGL driver and every other renderer supply a neutral tangent. CNA lists the limitation in {{src:handoff.md|handoff.md}} section 5.2.

issues.title: Matrix camera builders have no XNA oracle and no full-matrix value test
issues.summary: CreateLookAt and the perspective and orthographic builders are asserted only on single terms and covered indirectly by consumer tests; CNA's XNA matrix oracle does not include them.
issues.public_contract: Matrix::CreateLookAt, CreatePerspective, CreatePerspectiveFieldOfView, CreatePerspectiveOffCenter, CreateOrthographic and CreateOrthographicOffCenter
issues.expected: The evidence standard CNA applies to the rest of Matrix: bit comparison with the genuine XNA runtime through {{src:tests/reference/xna40/framework/matrix-oracle.txt|matrix-oracle.txt}} and MatrixOracleTests, or at least value tests of all sixteen terms for representative inputs.

At TARGET the direct evidence is:

  • in {{src:modules/math/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/MatrixTests.cpp|MatrixTests.cpp}}: CreateLookAtM44IsOne (M44 only), CreateOrthographicM11 (M11, M22, M44), CreateOrthographicOffCenterM44 (M44, M11), three …M34IsMinusOne cases for the perspective builders, and the thrown cases;

issues.title: BoundingSphere::CreateFromBoundingBox and the SmoothStep/Hermite/CatmullRom helpers use different arithmetic from XNA 4.0, and no oracle measures last-bit agreement
issues.summary: CreateFromBoundingBox and the SmoothStep/Hermite/CatmullRom helpers compute with formulas or precision that differ from XNA's, and only CreateFromPoints has an XNA oracle.
issues.public_contract: BoundingSphere::CreateFromBoundingBox; MathHelper::SmoothStep, Hermite, CatmullRom; Vector2/3/4::SmoothStep and Hermite
issues.expected: CNA's math module aims at XNA-exact results where they are cheap to reach, and backs that with oracle tests ({{src:modules/math/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/BoundingSphereOracleTests.cpp|BoundingSphereOracleTests.cpp}}, MatrixOracleTests.cpp).
issues.actual: BoundingSphere::CreateFromBoundingBox in {{src:modules/math/src/BoundingSphere.cpp|BoundingSphere.cpp}} computes the centre as (Min + Max) / 2 and the radius as Distance(center, Max); XNA uses Vector3.Lerp(Min, Max, 0.5f) and Vector3.Distance(Min, Max) * 0.5f. {{src:modules/math/src/MathHelper.cpp|MathHelper.cpp}} evaluates Hermite and CatmullRom in double (Hermite with endpoint shortcuts for amounts within machine epsilon of 0 or 1) and SmoothStep through that Hermite, whereas XNA's MathHelper computes all three in float: Lerp(value1, value2, t*t*(3 - 2t)) for SmoothStep and its own float polynomials for Hermite and CatmullRom. The vector SmoothStep forms (SmoothStepScalar in {{src:modules/math/src/Vector2.cpp|Vector2.cpp}}, Vector3.cpp and Vector4.cpp) evaluate the float Hermite basis with zero tangents, where XNA computes value1 + (value2 - value1) * (t*t*(3 - 2t)). The vector Hermite forms (HermiteScalar) use the same float polynomial and operation order as XNA's Vector2/3/4.Hermite, so there only the evaluation precision of the 32-bit x87 runtime could differ. Agreement in the last bit is plausible for many inputs but unmeasured.

issues.title: No test pins EffectParameter's divergences for CNA-constructed parameters, including a SetValue(Texture*) that GetValueTexture2D() does not read back
issues.summary: Parameters without compiled storage keep separate base and typed texture slots and refuse numeric access only for Object-class parameters; the C API smoke test exercises the lenient string, numeric and texture setters, but no test pins that a texture set through the base overload reads back as null, or that the numeric refusal is by class rather than by storage.
issues.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Graphics::EffectParameter SetValue/GetValue on stock-effect and standalone parameters
issues.expected: XNA rejects mismatched parameter access with InvalidCastException; CNA does so for compiled effects (FX-089/FX-105) and deliberately keeps a lenient mode for CNA-constructed parameters, which the C API's standalone-parameter tests rely on.
issues.actual: In {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/EffectParameter.cpp|EffectParameter.cpp}}, RequireNumericParameter runs first in every numeric accessor and refuses only Object-class parameters, whether or not the parameter has compiled storage, so its comment's carve-out for CNA-constructed parameters is really a class rule: a CNA-constructed Object-class parameter still refuses numeric access. When compiledStorage_ is null nothing else is checked: SetValue(const std::string&) stores the string whatever the record's type, numeric setters write floatData_ whatever the class, and SetValue(Texture*) writes textureData_ while GetValueTexture2D() returns texture2DData_, so a texture set through the base-class overload reads back as null (the header records the separate texture slots as an out-of-scope API-shape decision, Task 863).

• {{src:cmake/UnitTests.cmake|UnitTests.cmake}} removes those eight suites from CnaTests for every non-SDL3 audio selection, because they read SDL3_mixer's own track handles. For ALSA it keeps AudioCategoryTests. What exercises the XNA facade on CNA's mixer is therefore {{src:modules/audio/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Audio/CnaMixerXnaTests.cpp|CnaMixerXnaTests.cpp}} (seven cases: a fire-and-forget play, an instance playing for its duration, pause/resume/stop, a looped instance, a dynamic instance consuming buffers, which file formats load, and one end-to-end recording through ALSA's file device), {{src:modules/audio/tests/CNA/Internal/Audio/CnaMixerTests.cpp|CnaMixerTests.cpp}} (24 mixer-level cases), AudioCategoryTests (28 cases, twelve of which play cues from real SoundBank fixtures, nine with WaveBank-backed instances, and check pause, resume, stop, volume and instance-limit eviction through the public API), the microphone suites and one ALSA-only MediaPlayer song-end case. issues.title: The physical source-partition validator checks only *.cpp/*.mm path prefixes, so headers, C sources and a TU in a renderer's src/ subdirectory (never compiled) all pass it
issues.summary: modules/CMakeLists.txt's no-loss ownership gate globs only .cpp and .mm and compares path prefixes, while cna_add_renderer globs src/*.cpp non-recursively, so a new TU under src/<subdir>/ passes configure and is silently not built.
issues.public_contract: modules/CMakeLists.txt physical source-partition validator; modules/renderers/CMakeLists.txt cna_add_renderer
issues.expected: The validator's comment calls it a no-loss ownership gate: "file physical module location == declared CMake ownership" and "module CMakeLists glob exactly their own src/, so location IS ownership".
issues.actual: It runs file(GLOB_RECURSE ... "*.cpp" "*.mm") and only requires each path to start with a declared module's src|tests|examples|benchmarks prefix. Headers and .c files are never considered. cna_add_renderer() collects ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/*.cpp without recursion, so a TU placed in, say, src/detail/ satisfies the prefix check and is not compiled. Existing examples are intentional (standalone shader tools under directx9/src/shaders/ and common/d3d/src/shaders/), which is exactly why the gate cannot distinguish a deliberate exclusion from a lost file.

issues.title: A plain ctest run of the tests preset is not a trustworthy result
issues.summary: The tests preset builds only CnaTests, yet ctest also runs the display-dependent smoke executables the same configuration registers and reports the unbuilt ones as failed, so CNA's own preset calls a direct CnaTests run the only authoritative result.
issues.public_contract: ctest over a build of the tests preset (CMakePresets.json)
issues.expected: Every registered test either builds with the target the preset builds or is skipped, and test cases are isolated enough to run as separate processes in parallel.
issues.actual:
The tests preset builds only CnaTests (its build preset names that one target), yet ctest also runs the many separately registered display-dependent graphics smoke executables that the same configuration registers (CNA_BUILD_EXAMPLES is on, the default renderer is OPENGLES3) and reports the unbuilt ones as failures. CI does not hit either problem: general-tests-ci.yml runs a plain ctest, but only after a full default build and serially; the other jobs select labels or run the test binary.

Fixed since first recorded: the race. gtest_discover_tests still runs every CnaTests case as its own process, but the audio fixtures that shared fixed directories (cna_cue_test, cna_wavebank_test) are written under a per-process scratch root (CnaAudioTest::FixtureRoot, GSC-0008), every test process gets its own per-user data root (AM4-162), and the socket-opening suites hold one CTest RESOURCE_LOCK (AM4-163). issues.title: No test measures presentation cadence: PresentInterval::Two against ordinary vsync
issues.summary: The registered interval tests on EasyGL, SOFTWARE, SDL_GPU and WEBGPU and the shared forwarding contract check storage, forwarding and the selected present mode, not the resulting frame timing.
issues.public_contract: PresentationParameters.PresentationInterval (One, Two, Immediate) and the renderers' swap-interval / present-mode mapping
issues.expected: PresentInterval::Two means presenting every second vertical retrace (half refresh rate). Only a timing measurement shows that a renderer really does it.
issues.actual: The interval tests - {{src:modules/renderers/easygl/examples/easygl_present_interval_test.cpp|easygl_present_interval_test.cpp}} (also registered for SOFTWARE), {{src:modules/renderers/sdl-gpu/examples/sdlgpu_presentation_surface_test.cpp|sdlgpu_presentation_surface_test.cpp}}, {{src:modules/renderers/webgpu/examples/webgpu_present_mode_test.cpp|webgpu_present_mode_test.cpp}} and {{src:modules/graphics/examples/swap_interval_forwarding_contract_test.cpp|swap_interval_forwarding_contract_test.cpp}} (also run on SDL_GPU as a cross-family program) - assert what was requested, forwarded, recorded or which present mode was chosen. None times presents; the shared PresentInterval test says so itself (actual VSync timing is a display effect that cannot be verified headlessly). SDL_GPU cannot produce half rate through its API: it applies ordinary one-vblank vsync for Two and records the fallback (GetAppliedSwapIntervalEXT, pinned by sdlgpu_presentation_surface_test). A timing record would verify half rate only for the renderers that hand 2 to the driver, such as EasyGL and DIRECTX9 (D3DPRESENT_INTERVAL_TWO).

issues.title: Destroying a caller-created GraphicsDevice while resources on it are still live is allowed by cna_graphics_device_destroy but untested
issues.summary: graphics_device.h says resources on a caller-created device are released with it and the destroy route checks no child count, but every C test destroys the resources first, so what later calls on those resource handles do rests on reading.
issues.public_contract: cna_graphics_device_create / cna_graphics_device_destroy (CNA/C/graphics_device.h) and the resource handles created on a caller-created device
issues.expected: A sequence the header explicitly permits (destroying a caller-created device while resources made on it still exist) has a test that pins what happens to those resources and to their still-registered handles, and the header says whether each handle must still be destroyed.
issues.actual: cna_graphics_device_destroy resolves the OwnedGraphicsDevice, calls GraphicsDevice::Dispose() and releases the handle; it counts no children, by design (AddOwnedGraphicsResourceFor counts only game-owned resources so a standalone device cannot block cna_game_destroy). By reading, the C++ layer makes the order safe: GraphicsDevice::Dispose(bool) disposes every tracked resource, ~GraphicsDevice resets resourceDeviceLifetime_, a resource's later Dispose/destructor skips the device once that token has expired, and data routes that validate disposal (for example VertexBuffer's SetData validation) throw ObjectDisposedException, which the C exception barrier turns into a result. Handles are generation-checked, so the released device handle cannot be confused with a later one; cna_graphics_resource_get_graphics_device is refused for such a resource whether or not its device still exists (a separate entry). The resource handles stay registered until the caller destroys each one; the header's “released with it” does not say whether that call is still required. None of this is exercised: OwnedGraphicsDeviceSmoke.c destroys its texture before the device, CnbToolingSmoke.c its content manager first, and GameSecondaryGraphicsDeviceContextSmoke.c leaves no resource on the device it destroys.
